The benefit of selling to a local buyer is speed and transparency. You get same-day payment in cash, and you can ask questions about how they arrived at their offer. No waiting for shipping, no mystery grading, no middlemen.

If you’re selling inherited jewelry or estate diamonds, the process is the same. Bring it in, get it evaluated, and walk away with cash. If you’re downsizing your collection or going through a divorce, selling estate jewelry to a professional buyer takes the stress out of the process.

White Diamonds vs. Lab-Created Diamonds: What’s the Difference?

Lab-created diamonds look identical to natural white diamonds under a microscope, but they’re made in a lab rather than mined from the earth. They’re chemically and optically the same—the only difference is origin.

Lab diamonds are usually cheaper than natural diamonds of the same quality. But here’s the catch: they don’t hold value as well. If you ever want to sell a lab diamond, you’ll get less for it than you would for a natural diamond of the same carat weight and clarity.

If you’re buying for investment or heirloom purposes, natural white diamonds are the better choice. If you’re looking for something beautiful and affordable just to enjoy, a lab diamond might work.

How to Spot a Quality White Diamond

Even without a jeweler’s loupe, there are things you can check when looking at a white diamond in person.

  • Sparkle: A well-cut white diamond throws rainbow light (fire) and white light (brilliance). If it looks dull or lifeless, the cut might be poor.
  • Transparency: Hold it up to light. You should be able to see through it clearly without any brown or yellow tint.
  • Inclusions: Look for visible flaws or cloudiness. The cleaner it looks to the naked eye, the higher the clarity grade.
  • Certification: Always ask for a lab report. GIA, AGS, and other reputable labs stand behind their grading.

If something feels off about the diamond—if it looks yellow-ish, dull, or cloudy—trust your gut and walk away. There are plenty of beautiful white diamonds out there.

Should You Get Your White Diamond Appraised?

If you already own a white diamond and you’re thinking about selling it, yes—absolutely get it appraised. An appraisal tells you exactly what your diamond is worth based on its 4 Cs.

If you inherited a diamond or received one as a gift, an appraisal helps you understand what you have. It’s also useful for insurance purposes if something happens to the jewelry.

The good news is that getting a diamond appraisal in Los Angeles is free when you work with a reputable buyer. They’ll evaluate your stone and give you a fair cash offer with no pressure to sell.

People Also Ask About White Diamonds

The honest answer to where to go next: Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds.

Are white diamonds real?

Yes, white diamonds are completely real. They’re natural diamonds that have little to no color. The term “white” is a bit misleading—they’re actually colorless, which is what makes them valuable. Lab-created diamonds exist too, but natural white diamonds are the standard in fine jewelry.

What’s the difference between a white diamond and a clear diamond?

White and clear are basically the same thing when we’re talking about diamonds. Both terms describe colorless diamonds in the D-F color range. The terms are used interchangeably in the jewelry industry.

How much is a 1-carat white diamond worth?

A 1-carat white diamond typically costs between $3,000 and $12,000, depending on clarity, cut, and color grade. A high-quality stone (VS1 clarity, excellent cut, colorless) might run $8,000 to $12,000. A lower-quality stone (SI1 clarity, good cut) might be $3,000 to $5,000. Always compare certifications before buying.

Can you sell white diamonds for cash?

Absolutely. You can sell white diamond jewelry to local jewelers, pawn shops, or specialized buyers. The best option is working with a trusted buyer who offers fair pricing, professional evaluation, and same-day cash payment. If you’re in Los Angeles, contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds for a free appraisal and cash offer.

If you’re searching for a gold buyer in Downtown Los Angeles, you probably want more than someone who simply puts your jewelry on a scale and gives you a number.

You want to understand what you actually own, how it is being evaluated, what affects its value, and what you will actually receive if you decide to sell.

Downtown Los Angeles is home to one of the country’s best-known jewelry districts, giving sellers access to experienced buyers for gold jewelry, diamonds, coins, estate pieces, inherited collections, designer jewelry, and luxury watches.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds has served Los Angeles customers since 2007 and provides in-person evaluations at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014, in the Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District.

Whether you’re selling one unwanted gold ring or an entire estate collection, this guide explains what to know before choosing a Downtown Los Angeles gold buyer.

What Does a Gold Buyer in Downtown Los Angeles Evaluate?

A professional evaluation should start by determining exactly what you have.

Depending on the item, a buyer may consider:

  • Gold purity
  • Weight
  • Current gold market conditions
  • Diamonds and gemstones
  • Designer or brand
  • Condition
  • Age
  • Collectibility
  • Current resale demand
  • Original documentation
  • Whether the complete piece may be worth more than its gold content

For ordinary scrap gold, weight and purity may be the most important factors.

However, a diamond ring, designer bracelet, collectible coin, estate piece, or luxury watch may require a more complete evaluation.

That is why choosing a buyer who understands jewelry—not simply precious-metal weight—can make a difference.

If you’re trying to estimate your gold before visiting a buyer, see our complete guide to how much your gold is worth.

How Gold Purity Affects What Your Jewelry Is Worth

Gold jewelry is available in several purity levels.

Common examples include:

  • 10K gold — approximately 41.7% pure gold
  • 14K gold — approximately 58.3% pure gold
  • 18K gold — 75% pure gold
  • 22K gold — approximately 91.7% pure gold
  • 24K gold — approximately 99.9% pure gold

If two pieces have the same weight, the higher-karat piece generally contains more pure gold and therefore has a higher intrinsic precious-metal value.

But purity alone does not always determine what a piece is worth.

For example, a desirable designer bracelet could potentially have resale value beyond the underlying gold contained in the piece.

How Is the Current Gold Price Used?

Gold trades internationally, and its price can move throughout the trading day.

You can check current market information through an established precious-metals source such as GoldPrice.org.

The spot price provides an important reference point, but the price of pure gold should not automatically be confused with the cash amount someone will pay for finished jewelry.

Before making an offer, a buyer may need to determine:

  • What karat is the jewelry?
  • What does it actually weigh?
  • How much of that weight represents payable gold?
  • Does the piece contain gemstones or non-gold components?
  • Does it have designer, collectible, or resale value?
  • What are current market conditions for that particular item?

Only after evaluating the actual piece can a meaningful final offer be made.

What Percentage of Gold Value Can You Receive?

There is no single payout percentage that applies to every piece of jewelry.

Depending on the specific jewelry item and its complete evaluation, Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds may pay approximately 80–95% of the relevant gold value.

Where an item falls within that range can depend on factors such as:

  • Gold purity
  • Weight
  • Type of jewelry
  • Condition
  • Refining considerations
  • Diamonds or gemstones
  • Designer or brand
  • Resale potential
  • Current market demand

A broken 10K chain and a desirable 18K designer bracelet should not necessarily be evaluated the same way.

The most useful question is not simply:

“What percentage do you pay?”

Instead, ask:

“What are you paying for my specific item, and how did you calculate the offer?”

The Highest Gold Quote Isn’t Always the Best Offer

This is one of the most important things to understand before choosing a gold buyer.

The highest preliminary quote is not necessarily the highest amount you will actually receive.

Imagine calling several buyers before visiting them.

Three businesses give you similar estimates.

Then another buyer gives you a dramatically higher number.

Naturally, that higher number gets your attention.

It can also become the number against which you compare everything else.

This is known as anchoring. Once a strong number enters your mind, it can influence how every later offer feels.

You may then visit several other buyers.

They physically inspect your jewelry, test the purity, weigh the items, and make actual offers.

But because none of those offers matches the unusually high preliminary quote, you may think:

“The first buyer offered me more. I should go back there.”

When you return, however, the original quote may change after the jewelry is physically inspected.

The initial number may have been based on assumptions about weight, purity, condition, stones, or the type of item.

That does not mean every high quote is misleading. A buyer may legitimately be willing to pay more.

But sellers should understand the difference between:

a preliminary estimate

and

a final offer made after inspecting the actual item.

Compare Final Offer With Final Offer

When comparing gold buyers, ask:

  • Have you inspected my actual jewelry?
  • Is this an estimate or your final offer?
  • What purity did my jewelry test at?
  • What payable weight are you using?
  • What gold price are you using?
  • Are there any deductions?
  • Are diamonds or gemstones being valued separately?
  • Does the piece have designer or resale value?
  • What amount would I actually receive if I sold the item now?

The buyer who gives you the largest number first is not necessarily the buyer who will pay you the largest amount in the end.

Compare actual, item-specific final offers.

Why Transparent Gold Evaluation Matters

A good evaluation should allow you to understand the main factors behind the offer.

Gold Testing

The buyer determines whether the piece is gold and estimates its purity.

A stamp such as 10K, 14K, 18K, 417, 585, or 750 can provide useful information, but professional testing may still be appropriate.

Weighing

Gold jewelry is commonly weighed in grams.

You should understand the weight being used to calculate your offer.

Identifying Non-Gold Components

Some jewelry contains:

  • Gemstones
  • Springs
  • Steel components
  • Watch movements
  • Non-gold clasps
  • Other materials

The gross weight of a piece does not necessarily represent its payable gold weight.

Evaluating Additional Value

Some jewelry may have value beyond its gold content.

This can include:

  • Diamonds
  • Designer jewelry
  • Estate pieces
  • Antique jewelry
  • Collectible items
  • Certain luxury watches
  • Certain coins

Final Offer

Once the jewelry has actually been inspected, the buyer can make an item-specific offer.

You should then be able to decide whether that offer makes sense for you.

What Can You Sell to a Downtown Los Angeles Gold Buyer?

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates many categories of jewelry and valuables.

Gold Jewelry

Items can include:

  • Gold rings
  • Gold necklaces
  • Gold chains
  • Gold bracelets
  • Gold earrings
  • Wedding bands
  • Broken jewelry
  • Scrap gold
  • 10K gold
  • 14K gold
  • 18K gold
  • 22K gold

If jewelry is what you’re selling, see our complete guide to selling gold jewelry in Los Angeles.

Broken and Scrap Gold

Broken jewelry can still contain valuable precious metal.

A damaged clasp does not remove the gold from a chain.

A bent ring can still retain its underlying gold value.

Common scrap-gold items include:

  • Broken chains
  • Damaged bracelets
  • Single earrings
  • Bent rings
  • Old wedding bands
  • Jewelry missing stones
  • Outdated jewelry
  • Unwanted gold pieces

Before throwing damaged gold away, have it evaluated.

Gold Coins and Bullion

Coins should not always be evaluated in the same way as ordinary jewelry.

Some gold coins are primarily valued according to their metal content.

Others can potentially have:

  • Numismatic value
  • Collectible premiums
  • Scarcity
  • Historical significance
  • Condition-related premiums

If you’re selling coins, read our guide to finding a gold coin buyer in Downtown Los Angeles.

Diamond Jewelry

If your gold jewelry contains diamonds, the stones may deserve separate consideration.

For example, an 18K engagement ring could potentially involve:

gold value + diamond value + potential resale value of the complete ring

The diamond should not automatically be ignored simply because the gold setting is also being evaluated.

For loose diamonds and diamond jewelry, visit our diamond buyer and evaluation page.

Estate Jewelry

Estate collections frequently contain a mixture of valuables.

A collection might include:

  • Gold jewelry
  • Platinum
  • Diamond jewelry
  • Designer pieces
  • Watches
  • Coins
  • Antique jewelry
  • Sterling silver
  • Collectible pieces

Before treating an estate collection as scrap, the individual pieces should be identified.

Read our Los Angeles estate jewelry selling guide for more information.

Inherited Jewelry

Inherited jewelry can be especially difficult to evaluate because you may not know what the original owner purchased.

One box could contain ordinary gold beside a valuable diamond, designer bracelet, gold coin, or luxury watch.

Avoid assuming everything should be grouped together and sold by weight.

Our guide to selling inherited jewelry with no obligation explains what to consider before selling an inherited collection.

Luxury Watches

Rolex and other luxury watches should generally not be valued simply according to their gold weight.

A luxury watch evaluation can involve:

  • Brand
  • Model
  • Reference number
  • Age
  • Condition
  • Originality
  • Movement
  • Bracelet
  • Box
  • Papers
  • Current demand

If you’re selling a Rolex, see our Rolex Buyer Los Angeles guide.

Pawn Shop vs. Gold Buyer in Downtown Los Angeles

Pawn shops and dedicated gold buyers serve somewhat different purposes.

Pawn shops typically provide both:

  • Collateral loans
  • Outright purchases

A specialized jewelry and precious-metal buyer focuses primarily on evaluating and purchasing valuables.

That does not mean every pawn shop gives a poor offer.

It also does not mean every gold buyer automatically gives a better one.

The important thing is to compare:

the actual final offer for the exact same item.

For a deeper comparison, see our guide to the 10K gold price per gram at a pawn shop.

Local Gold Buyer vs. Online Gold Buyer

Both local and online buyers can be legitimate options.

The difference is mainly in how the evaluation and transaction take place.

Advantages of an In-Person Evaluation

Selling locally allows you to:

  • Keep possession of the jewelry until you make a decision
  • See the item being examined
  • Ask questions during the evaluation
  • Discuss the offer directly
  • Understand the final offer before accepting it

Online Gold Buyers

Online buyers can be convenient, especially for sellers who do not live near a major jewelry market.

However, the item generally needs to be shipped before the buyer can physically inspect it and provide a final item-specific offer.

Neither approach is automatically best for everyone.

Consider convenience, security, timing, transparency, and your comfort with the evaluation process.

Read our complete comparison of local gold buyers vs. online gold buyers.

What Should You Bring to a Gold Evaluation?

Bring the jewelry or valuables you want evaluated.

If you have relevant paperwork, bring that as well.

Useful documentation can include:

  • Original receipts
  • Diamond grading reports
  • Designer certificates
  • Watch boxes and papers
  • Previous appraisals
  • Coin documentation
  • Estate records

Documentation does not automatically increase the value of an item.

However, it can sometimes help identify or authenticate diamonds, designer pieces, luxury watches, coins, or estate jewelry.

You should also bring any identification required for the transaction.

Should You Clean Your Gold Before Selling?

Usually, you do not need to aggressively clean jewelry before having it evaluated.

Cleaning ordinary scrap gold does not increase the amount of gold contained in the piece.

Improper cleaning or polishing can potentially damage:

  • Antique jewelry
  • Certain gemstones
  • Special finishes
  • Designer pieces
  • Collectible jewelry

If you’re unsure what you have, let the buyer inspect it first.

Why Downtown Los Angeles Is Important for Gold Sellers

Downtown Los Angeles has long been one of the country’s major jewelry and precious-metal markets.

The Jewelry District contains a concentration of:

  • Gold buyers
  • Jewelers
  • Diamond dealers
  • Watch specialists
  • Estate jewelry buyers
  • Precious-metal businesses

For sellers, having many jewelry-related businesses in the same area can make researching and comparing buyers easier.

  2. What weight are you using?
  3. What gold market price are you using?

  8. Are there any fees or deductions?
  9. Am I free to decline the offer?
  10. What amount would I actually receive?

These questions can tell you more about a transaction than simply asking:

“Who says they pay the highest?”

Red Flags When Choosing a Gold Buyer

Be cautious if a buyer:

  • Refuses to explain how the offer was calculated
  • Will not explain the weight or purity
  • Creates unnecessary pressure to sell immediately
  • Gives an unusually high preliminary quote and cannot explain why the final amount changed
  • Is vague about deductions
  • Automatically ignores potentially valuable diamonds
  • Treats obvious designer jewelry as scrap without examining it
  • Makes guarantees before inspecting what you own

The goal is not simply to hear the largest number.

The goal is to understand the strongest real offer for your actual item.

mainHtml:
White gold looks like silver, but here’s the thing — it’s actually just as valuable as yellow gold. That’s because white gold is an alloy, meaning it’s a blend of yellow gold mixed with other white metals like nickel or palladium. The result? A gorgeous silvery-white metal that keeps all the value and durability you expect from gold.

If you own white gold jewelry, a luxury watch, or inherited pieces and you’re wondering what they’re worth, this guide breaks down exactly what white gold is, how it’s made, and why it matters when you’re thinking about selling.

Related: How to Know if Diamonds Are Worth Selling: 7 Key Factors

Related: How Much Should I Get for My Gold Jewelry? 2026 Guide

What Exactly Is White Gold?

White gold starts as regular yellow gold. But instead of staying yellow, jewelers mix it with other metals to create that white, silvery look you see in modern jewelry.

Related: White Gold vs Yellow Gold: Which Is Better for You?

The most common metals blended into white gold are:

Related: Platinum vs White Gold: Which Metal Is Right for You?

  • Nickel – adds whiteness and strength
  • Palladium – a precious metal that makes it hypoallergenic (great if you have sensitive skin)
  • Copper and Zinc – helps with durability and workability

So when you see a white gold ring, you’re looking at yellow gold that’s been mixed with these other metals to get that clean, modern white finish. It’s not painted on or plated permanently — it’s part of the metal itself.

Understanding Purity and Carats

White gold is measured in carats just like yellow gold. The purity tells you exactly how much actual gold is in the piece.

Common white gold purities are:

  • 24K gold – 100% pure gold (rarely used for jewelry because it’s too soft)
  • 18K gold – 75% gold, 25% other metals (high quality, holds value well)
  • 14K gold – 58.3% gold, 41.7% other metals (the most popular for rings and everyday jewelry)
  • 10K gold – 41.7% gold, 58.3% other metals (affordable, but contains less actual gold)

The higher the karat number, the more gold is in the piece, and the more valuable it is. If you’re selling white gold jewelry, knowing the karat weight is crucial because it directly affects what buyers will pay.

Rhodium Plating: The Secret to That Shine

Here’s something most people don’t know: white gold jewelry is usually coated with a thin layer of rhodium. Rhodium is a precious metal that makes white gold look whiter, brighter, and more durable.

Over time, rhodium plating can wear off — especially on rings you wear every day. When that happens, your white gold might start to look slightly yellowish or dull. That’s completely normal and doesn’t mean your jewelry is damaged.

Related: Best 14K White Gold Rings 2026: Top 5 Ranked & Compared

You can have rhodium replating done at a jeweler, but if you’re thinking about selling your piece, don’t worry about it. When Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates your white gold jewelry, we look at the actual gold content, not the plating condition.

Explore Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds →

White Gold vs. Yellow Gold: What’s the Difference in Value?

This is a big question people ask: is white gold worth more or less than yellow gold?

The answer is straightforward — they’re worth the same. A white gold ring and a yellow gold ring with the same karat weight and gold content will have nearly identical gold value.

The price difference comes down to:

  • Style and fashion trends – white gold has been trendy for the last 15+ years, so there’s higher demand
  • The alloy metals used – if your white gold contains palladium instead of nickel, it might be worth slightly more because palladium is a precious metal
  • Design and craftsmanship – a beautifully designed piece is worth more than a simple one, regardless of color
  • Attached gemstones – diamonds or other precious stones can significantly increase value

If you’re curious about comparing white gold to other precious metals, check out our guide on platinum vs white gold to see how they stack up.

Why White Gold Became So Popular

White gold didn’t always dominate the jewelry market. A few decades ago, yellow gold was king. But starting in the 1980s and especially through the 2000s and 2010s, white gold became the metal of choice for engagement rings, wedding bands, and everyday jewelry.

Why the shift? A few reasons:

  • Modern aesthetic – white gold looks contemporary and sleek
  • Works better with diamonds – the white metal makes white diamonds look even more brilliant
  • Versatile style – pairs well with both casual and formal outfits
  • Celebrity influence – Hollywood celebrities drove demand for white gold engagement rings

This popularity means if you own white gold jewelry, there’s strong demand for it if you decide to sell. That’s good news for your resale value.

What to Know If You’re Selling White Gold

If you inherited white gold jewelry, are downsizing your collection, or just need cash, here’s what matters:

First, know what you have. Check for hallmarks or stamps inside the jewelry that indicate the karat weight (10K, 14K, 18K, etc.). If there’s no stamp, a professional evaluation is necessary.

Second, understand that the value comes from the gold content, not the brand name or how new it looks. A scratched 18K white gold ring from an unknown jeweler is worth more than a pristine 10K white gold ring because it contains more actual gold.

Third, get it professionally appraised. At Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, we provide free, no-obligation evaluations. We test the metal, weigh it, calculate the current gold price, and make a fair offer on the spot. Same-day payment, no pressure.

If you’re looking to sell white gold jewelry or diamonds in Los Angeles, our team has been buying precious metals since 2007. We treat every piece with care and every customer with respect. Learn more about how to sell your gold jewelry in downtown Los Angeles.

Caring for Your White Gold Jewelry

If you still own white gold pieces and want to keep them looking beautiful, here’s what helps:

  • Clean gently – use warm soapy water and a soft cloth, not harsh chemicals
  • Store safely – keep it in a soft pouch or jewelry box to avoid scratches
  • Wear wisely – remove white gold rings before working out, gardening, or doing dishes
  • Get it checked – if a stone starts to loosen, have it fixed right away

These simple steps help your white gold stay beautiful longer. But remember — even if your pieces get worn or dinged up, they’re still valuable because of the gold content. Condition doesn’t change the gold price.

White Gold With Diamonds and Gemstones

A lot of white gold jewelry features diamonds or other gemstones. That’s where the real value often lives.

A white gold band by itself is worth the spot price of gold times the weight. But add a diamond, and you’re looking at significantly more value. Diamonds are graded on the four Cs: cut, color, clarity, and carat weight. If you have a 14K white gold diamond ring, both the gold and the stone have value.

If you’re selling pieces with gemstones, get them professionally evaluated. We can help with that at Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds — we handle diamond appraisals and offer free diamond appraisals in Los Angeles.

Common Questions About White Gold

Does white gold tarnish or turn yellow over time?

White gold itself doesn’t tarnish. However, the rhodium plating on top can wear away with time and wear, making the underlying gold show through slightly. This looks like the jewelry is turning yellowish or dull. It’s cosmetic, not structural damage. You can have it replated, or you can sell it as-is — the gold value remains the same.

Is white gold hypoallergenic?

It depends on what metals are mixed with the gold. If your white gold contains palladium or platinum-group metals, it’s likely hypoallergenic. If it contains nickel, some people with nickel allergies might experience a reaction. If you have sensitive skin and aren’t sure, get your jewelry tested or ask the original jeweler what’s in the alloy.

Can I sell white gold jewelry without the original receipt or certificate?

Absolutely. You don’t need paperwork or proof of purchase to sell white gold. A professional buyer tests the metal directly, verifies the purity, and weighs it to calculate value. That’s all that matters. If your piece has diamonds or gemstones, a certificate helps establish value, but it’s not required.

What’s the difference between white gold and platinum?

Great question. Platinum is denser, more durable, and more expensive than white gold. It doesn’t require rhodium plating because it naturally maintains its white color. If you want to understand the full comparison, we’ve broken down platinum vs white gold in detail. For now, know that both are valuable precious metals.

If you’re looking to sell white gold jewelry or diamonds in Los Angeles, our team has been buying precious metals since 2007. We treat every piece with care and every customer with respect. Learn more about how to sell your gold jewelry in downtown Los Angeles. Caring for Your White Gold Jewelry If you still own white gold pieces and want to keep them looking beautiful, here’s what helps: Clean gently – use warm soapy water and a soft cloth, not harsh chemicals Store safely – keep it in a soft pouch or jewelry box to avoid scratches Wear wisely – remove white gold rings before working out, gardening, or doing dishes Get it checked – if a stone starts to loosen, have it fixed right away These simple steps help your white gold stay beautiful longer. But remember — even if your pieces get worn or dinged up, they’re still valuable because of the gold content. Condition doesn’t change the gold price. White Gold With Diamonds and Gemstones A lot of white gold jewelry features diamonds or other gemstones. That’s where the real value often lives. A white gold band by itself is worth the spot price of gold times the weight. But add a diamond, and you’re looking at significantly more value. Diamonds are graded on the four Cs: cut, color, clarity, and carat weight. If you have a 14K white gold diamond ring, both the gold and the stone have value. If you’re selling pieces with gemstones, get them professionally evaluated. We can help with that at Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds — we handle diamond appraisals and offer free diamond appraisals in Los Angeles. Common Questions About White Gold Does white gold tarnish or turn yellow over time? White gold itself doesn’t tarnish. However, the rhodium plating on top can wear away with time and wear, making the underlying gold show through slightly. This looks like the jewelry is turning yellowish or dull. It’s cosmetic, not structural damage. You can have it replated, or you can sell it as-is — the gold value remains the same. Is white gold hypoallergenic? It depends on what metals are mixed with the gold. If your white gold contains palladium or platinum-group metals, it’s likely hypoallergenic. If it contains nickel, some people with nickel allergies might experience a reaction. If you have sensitive skin and aren’t sure, get your jewelry tested or ask the original jeweler what’s in the alloy. Can I sell white gold jewelry without the original receipt or certificate? Absolutely. You don’t need paperwork or proof of purchase to sell white gold. A professional buyer tests the metal directly, verifies the purity, and weighs it to calculate value. That’s all that matters. If your piece has diamonds or gemstones, a certificate helps establish value, but it’s not required. What’s the difference between white gold and platinum? Great question. Platinum is denser, more durable, and more expensive than white gold. It doesn’t require rhodium plating because it naturally maintains its white color. If you want to understand the full comparison, we’ve broken down platinum vs white gold in detail. For now, know that both are valuable precious metals. Best Place to Sell Gold Jewelry in Los Angeles: How to Get a Fair Price

If you have gold jewelry you no longer wear, the most important question is not simply “Who gives the highest quote?” It is “Who will give me the strongest real offer after actually evaluating my jewelry?”

For Los Angeles sellers, the best place to sell gold jewelry is generally an established buyer who can evaluate your items in person, explain the weight and purity, compare the value with the current gold market, and make a clear final offer without pressure.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds has served Los Angeles gold, diamond and jewelry sellers since 2007 from its Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District location at 617 S. Hill Street, Los Angeles, CA 90014.

This guide explains how gold jewelry is valued, where you can sell it, what affects the final offer, and how to compare buyers before making a decision.

Where Is the Best Place to Sell Gold Jewelry in Los Angeles?

Los Angeles sellers generally have three choices: a dedicated gold and jewelry buyer, a pawn shop, or an online/mail-in buyer.

For many sellers, an established local gold buyer provides the best combination of convenience, transparency and the ability to compare an actual offer before handing over valuable jewelry.

Dedicated Gold and Jewelry Buyers

A professional gold buyer evaluates jewelry specifically for its precious-metal content and, when appropriate, its potential resale value.

During an in-person evaluation, you should be able to ask:

  • What karat is my jewelry?
  • What does it weigh?
  • What gold price are you using?
  • Are stones or other non-gold components being deducted from the weight?
  • Does the piece have value beyond its gold content?
  • What is the final amount you will actually pay me?

For sellers who want to understand the Downtown Los Angeles market specifically, see our guide to selling gold jewelry in Downtown Los Angeles.

Pawn Shops

Pawn shops can be convenient, especially when someone wants either a collateral loan or a quick sale.

However, a pawn shop handles many categories of merchandise and may not specialize in precious-metal buying to the same degree as a dedicated gold buyer.

If maximizing the sale price is important, compare the pawn shop’s final purchase offer with an offer from a buyer that regularly evaluates gold jewelry.

Online Gold Buyers

Mail-in gold buyers provide another option, especially for sellers who do not live near a competitive jewelry market.

The tradeoff is that you normally need to package and ship your valuables, wait for an evaluation and then decide whether to accept the company’s offer.

Los Angeles sellers have the advantage of being able to visit the Downtown Jewelry District and receive in-person evaluations without shipping their jewelry across the country.

How Much Is Gold Jewelry Worth?

The starting point for determining the value of ordinary gold jewelry is relatively straightforward:

Gold content × weight × current gold price = approximate theoretical metal value.

The actual purchase offer can then differ based on refining costs, buyer margins, stones or non-gold components, market conditions, and whether the jewelry itself has additional resale value.

 

The three most important factors are purity, weight and the current gold market.

Gold Purity

Gold jewelry is usually marked by karat.

24K gold is close to pure gold.

22K gold is approximately 91.7% gold.

18K gold is 75% gold.

14K gold is approximately 58.5% gold.

10K gold is approximately 41.7% gold.

A professional buyer should verify the purity rather than relying entirely on a stamp because jewelry can be altered, repaired or incorrectly marked.

Weight

Gold jewelry is normally evaluated by weight, but the gross weight of a piece does not necessarily equal its pure-gold weight.

Stones, clasps, non-gold components and other materials may need to be taken into account.

This is one reason sellers should ask the buyer to explain how the calculation was made.

Current Gold Price

Gold prices change throughout the trading day.

Instead of relying on an old article or a fixed price posted months earlier, check a current precious-metals market source such as Kitco’s live gold price before visiting a buyer.

You can also learn more about how purity affects pricing in our guide to the 14K gold price per gram in Los Angeles.

Spot Price Is Not the Same as the Amount You Will Receive

This is one of the most important concepts for gold sellers to understand.

The spot price represents the market price of pure gold. It does not automatically mean a buyer will pay 100% of spot value for used jewelry.

For example, 14K jewelry contains approximately 58.5% gold, so the starting metal calculation is already different from the price of one gram of pure 24K gold.

The buyer must also account for refining, processing, market risk and operating costs.

That does not mean you should accept any offer.

It means the best comparison is between the final dollar amounts buyers are actually prepared to pay for the same jewelry, not simply an advertised percentage, phone estimate or claim to pay “top dollar.”

Be Careful With Extremely High Initial Quotes

The highest quoted number is not necessarily the highest amount you will actually receive.

This is especially important when comparing phone quotes or preliminary estimates.

A buyer cannot accurately know the final value of most jewelry without verifying important details such as weight, purity, stones, condition and authenticity.

An unusually high quote may get your attention, but what matters is what happens after the jewelry is examined.

Ask each buyer for the final item-specific offer and how the offer was calculated.

If one company quotes dramatically more than everyone else before seeing the jewelry, do not automatically assume it will produce the highest final payout.

Compare real offers after evaluation.

The goal is not to find the buyer willing to say the biggest number.

The goal is to find the strongest legitimate offer for the jewelry you actually own.

For a deeper explanation, see How Much Is My Gold Worth? Gold Buyers Ranked.

Does Designer Gold Jewelry Have More Value Than Its Gold Weight?

Sometimes.

Ordinary broken chains, mismatched earrings and generic gold jewelry may primarily be valued for their precious-metal content.

But jewelry from brands such as Cartier, Tiffany & Co., Van Cleef & Arpels or other recognized luxury houses may have substantial resale value above melt value.

The same can apply to signed vintage jewelry, unusual estate pieces and collectible designs.

If you have designer jewelry, make sure the buyer evaluates the piece as jewelry before treating it simply as scrap gold.

For brand-specific information, see our guides to selling Tiffany jewelry in Los Angeles and selling Cartier jewelry in Los Angeles.

What About Gold Jewelry With Diamonds?

Gold jewelry containing diamonds should not automatically be valued as gold alone.

Depending on the diamonds’ size, quality and marketability, the stones may have separate value.

If you already have a GIA Diamond Grading Report, bring it with you.

A GIA report documents characteristics including carat weight, color, clarity and cut where applicable. It is important to understand that a GIA grading report is not a monetary appraisal. GIA grades and identifies diamonds but does not assign a resale value to them.

If your jewelry contains a meaningful natural diamond, ask whether the buyer is making a separate offer for the diamond in addition to the gold mounting.

Selling Inherited or Estate Gold Jewelry

Inherited jewelry can be difficult to evaluate because sellers may not know what is genuine gold, what is plated, which stones are valuable, or whether certain pieces are collectible.

You also may not have receipts, original packaging or previous appraisals.

That is normal.

A practical approach is to have the collection evaluated piece by piece.

Some pieces may primarily have gold value. Others may contain diamonds, be made from platinum, come from a designer brand or have estate-jewelry resale value.

You should also be able to decide which items you want to sell and which pieces you prefer to keep for sentimental reasons.

Avoid selling an entire inherited collection as one unexplained bulk number unless you clearly understand what is included in the offer.

Do You Need a Receipt to Sell Gold Jewelry in California?

A purchase receipt or original jewelry appraisal generally is not what determines whether your gold can be evaluated.

However, sellers should expect a legitimate secondhand dealer to verify identification as part of the transaction.

California rules governing secondhand dealers require seller identification information to be recorded and maintained.

Therefore, bring a valid government-issued photo ID when you visit.

If you also have useful documentation—such as a previous jewelry appraisal, designer paperwork, luxury-brand box or a GIA Diamond Grading Report—bring it with you because it may help identify or evaluate certain items.

Documentation can be helpful, but the jewelry itself still needs to be examined.

Should You Get an Appraisal Before Selling Gold?

Usually, you do not need to pay for a formal insurance appraisal just to sell ordinary gold jewelry.

Insurance appraisals and actual resale offers serve different purposes.

An insurance appraisal may estimate replacement cost, which can be substantially higher than what someone will pay to purchase the jewelry from you.

For ordinary gold jewelry, getting several real purchase offers can often tell you more about current resale value than paying for another retail replacement appraisal.

For unusually valuable estate jewelry, important designer pieces or significant diamonds, additional professional evaluation may make sense before selling.

Gold Buyer vs. Jewelry Store: Which Is Better?

Neither is automatically better for every piece.

A dedicated gold buyer may be particularly competitive for ordinary gold chains, rings, bracelets, earrings, scrap gold and broken jewelry because the business regularly purchases precious metals.

A jewelry store may be more interested in certain pieces that can be resold directly as finished jewelry.

A specialist may be the better choice for important designer jewelry, diamonds, collectible watches or rare estate pieces.

The important question is not what the business calls itself.

It is whether the buyer understands the specific item you are selling and can explain the final offer.

How to Compare Gold Buyers in Los Angeles

When you compare buyers, use the same jewelry each time and compare the actual final offer, not advertising claims.

Pay attention to whether the buyer weighs and tests your jewelry in front of you, explains the karat and weight, answers questions, identifies potentially valuable diamonds or designer pieces, clearly states the final amount and allows you to decline without pressure.

You can also research established buyers before visiting.

See our comparison guide to the best gold buyers in Los Angeles for additional information.

Why Sell Gold Jewelry in Downtown Los Angeles?

Downtown Los Angeles is home to one of the country’s major jewelry districts.

 

That concentration of jewelry businesses gives local sellers an important advantage: competition.

Instead of shipping jewelry to an unknown buyer or relying on a single estimate, you can compare different businesses within the same market.

For people in Beverly Hills, West Los Angeles, Hollywood, Pasadena, Glendale, Burbank, the San Fernando Valley, South Bay and surrounding communities, Downtown Los Angeles can also be a practical place to obtain an in-person evaluation.

Sell Gold Jewelry to Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds in Los Angeles

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds provides in-person evaluations for gold jewelry and other valuables in Downtown Los Angeles.

The business has served Los Angeles customers since 2007 and evaluates items including 10K, 14K, 18K and 22K gold jewelry, broken and scrap gold, diamond jewelry, designer jewelry, inherited and estate jewelry, gold coins, diamonds and luxury watches.

Evaluations are available without an obligation to sell.

If you decide the final offer makes sense for you, same-day purchase and payment are available.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds
617 S. Hill Street
Los Angeles, CA 90014
Phone: 310-663-1340

Visit Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds

Frequently Asked Questions About Selling Gold Jewelry in Los Angeles

What is the best place to sell gold jewelry in Los Angeles?

For many sellers, an established local gold and jewelry buyer is a strong option because the jewelry can be weighed, tested and evaluated in person. Compare actual final offers and choose a buyer who clearly explains how the price was calculated.

How is 14K gold jewelry valued?

14K gold is approximately 58.5% pure gold. Its starting metal value depends on the jewelry’s weight and the current gold price. The final purchase offer can also reflect refining costs, non-gold components, market conditions and whether the piece has additional resale value.

Is 18K gold worth more than 14K gold?

Per gram, 18K gold normally has more intrinsic gold value because it contains approximately 75% gold compared with about 58.5% for 14K gold.

Can I sell broken gold jewelry?

Yes. Broken chains, single earrings, damaged rings and other scrap gold can still contain significant precious-metal value even if the jewelry can no longer be worn.

Can I sell gold without a receipt?

A purchase receipt is generally not necessary simply to have gold jewelry evaluated, but legitimate secondhand dealers are required to verify seller identification. Bring valid government-issued photo identification.

Should I clean my gold before selling it?

Usually not. Cleaning does not change the amount of gold in the piece, and aggressive cleaning can potentially damage gemstones, finishes or collectible jewelry. Let the buyer evaluate the item in its current condition.

Should I accept the highest phone quote?

Not automatically. A preliminary quote made before a buyer verifies your jewelry may change after inspection. Compare the final dollar amount each buyer is actually prepared to pay after examining the item.

Does a GIA report tell me how much my diamond is worth?

No. A GIA Diamond Grading Report describes and grades the diamond’s characteristics. It does not assign a monetary appraisal or guarantee a resale price.

Can designer jewelry be worth more than melt value?

Yes. Cartier, Tiffany & Co. and other desirable designer jewelry may have resale value above its precious-metal content. Have recognized designer pieces evaluated as jewelry before agreeing to sell them only for scrap value.

Get a Real Offer Before You Decide

Selling gold jewelry should not require guessing.

Know what you have, understand how the buyer calculates the value, compare actual offers and make your decision only after you know the final amount you would receive.

If you’re in Los Angeles, you can bring your gold jewelry to Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds at 617 S. Hill Street in Downtown Los Angeles for an in-person evaluation and decide afterward whether selling makes sense for you.

It means the best comparison is between the final dollar amounts buyers are actually prepared to pay for the same jewelry, not simply an advertised percentage, phone estimate or claim to pay “top dollar.” Be Careful With Extremely High Initial Quotes The highest quoted number is not necessarily the highest amount you will actually receive. Compare final item-specific offers—not just preliminary phone quotes—when choosing where to sell gold jewelry. This is especially important when comparing phone quotes or preliminary estimates. A buyer cannot accurately know the final value of most jewelry without verifying important details such as weight, purity, stones, condition and authenticity. An unusually high quote may get your attention, but what matters is what happens after the jewelry is examined. Ask each buyer for the final item-specific offer and how the offer was calculated. If one company quotes dramatically more than everyone else before seeing the jewelry, do not automatically assume it will produce the highest final payout. Compare real offers after evaluation. The goal is not to find the buyer willing to say the biggest number. The goal is to find the strongest legitimate offer for the jewelry you actually own. For a deeper explanation, see How Much Is My Gold Worth? Gold Buyers Ranked. Does Designer Gold Jewelry Have More Value Than Its Gold Weight? Sometimes. Ordinary broken chains, mismatched earrings and generic gold jewelry may primarily be valued for their precious-metal content. But jewelry from brands such as Cartier, Tiffany & Co., Van Cleef & Arpels or other recognized luxury houses may have substantial resale value above melt value. The same can apply to signed vintage jewelry, unusual estate pieces and collectible designs. If you have designer jewelry, make sure the buyer evaluates the piece as jewelry before treating it simply as scrap gold. For brand-specific information, see our guides to selling Tiffany jewelry in Los Angeles and selling Cartier jewelry in Los Angeles. What About Gold Jewelry With Diamonds? Gold jewelry containing diamonds should not automatically be valued as gold alone. Depending on the diamonds’ size, quality and marketability, the stones may have separate value. If you already have a GIA Diamond Grading Report, bring it with you. A GIA report documents characteristics including carat weight, color, clarity and cut where applicable. It is important to understand that a GIA grading report is not a monetary appraisal. GIA grades and identifies diamonds but does not assign a resale value to them. If your jewelry contains a meaningful natural diamond, ask whether the buyer is making a separate offer for the diamond in addition to the gold mounting. Selling Inherited or Estate Gold Jewelry Inherited jewelry can be difficult to evaluate because sellers may not know what is genuine gold, what is plated, which stones are valuable, or whether certain pieces are collectible. You also may not have receipts, original packaging or previous appraisals. That is normal. A practical approach is to have the collection evaluated piece by piece. Some pieces may primarily have gold value. Others may contain diamonds, be made from platinum, come from a designer brand or have estate-jewelry resale value. You should also be able to decide which items you want to sell and which pieces you prefer to keep for sentimental reasons. Avoid selling an entire inherited collection as one unexplained bulk number unless you clearly understand what is included in the offer. Do You Need a Receipt to Sell Gold Jewelry in California? A purchase receipt or original jewelry appraisal generally is not what determines whether your gold can be evaluated. However, sellers should expect a legitimate secondhand dealer to verify identification as part of the transaction. California rules governing secondhand dealers require seller identification information to be recorded and maintained. Therefore, bring a valid government-issued photo ID when you visit. If you also have useful documentation—such as a previous jewelry appraisal, designer paperwork, luxury-brand box or a GIA Diamond Grading Report—bring it with you because it may help identify or evaluate certain items. Documentation can be helpful, but the jewelry itself still needs to be examined. Should You Get an Appraisal Before Selling Gold? Usually, you do not need to pay for a formal insurance appraisal just to sell ordinary gold jewelry. Insurance appraisals and actual resale offers serve different purposes. An insurance appraisal may estimate replacement cost, which can be substantially higher than what someone will pay to purchase the jewelry from you. For ordinary gold jewelry, getting several real purchase offers can often tell you more about current resale value than paying for another retail replacement appraisal. For unusually valuable estate jewelry, important designer pieces or significant diamonds, additional professional evaluation may make sense before selling. Gold Buyer vs. Jewelry Store: Which Is Better? Neither is automatically better for every piece. A dedicated gold buyer may be particularly competitive for ordinary gold chains, rings, bracelets, earrings, scrap gold and broken jewelry because the business regularly purchases precious metals. A jewelry store may be more interested in certain pieces that can be resold directly as finished jewelry. A specialist may be the better choice for important designer jewelry, diamonds, collectible watches or rare estate pieces. The important question is not what the business calls itself. It is whether the buyer understands the specific item you are selling and can explain the final offer. How to Compare Gold Buyers in Los Angeles When you compare buyers, use the same jewelry each time and compare the actual final offer, not advertising claims. Pay attention to whether the buyer weighs and tests your jewelry in front of you, explains the karat and weight, answers questions, identifies potentially valuable diamonds or designer pieces, clearly states the final amount and allows you to decline without pressure. You can also research established buyers before visiting. See our comparison guide to the best gold buyers in Los Angeles for additional information. Why Sell Gold Jewelry in Downtown Los Angeles? Downtown Los Angeles is home to one of the country’s major jewelry districts. Downtown Los Angeles gives gold sellers access to a competitive jewelry market where they can compare in-person evaluations and offers. That concentration of jewelry businesses gives local sellers an important advantage: competition. Instead of shipping jewelry to an unknown buyer or relying on a single estimate, you can compare different businesses within the same market. For people in Beverly Hills, West Los Angeles, Hollywood, Pasadena, Glendale, Burbank, the San Fernando Valley, South Bay and surrounding communities, Downtown Los Angeles can also be a practical place to obtain an in-person evaluation. The business has served Los Angeles customers since 2007 and evaluates items including 10K, 14K, 18K and 22K gold jewelry, broken and scrap gold, diamond jewelry, designer jewelry, inherited and estate jewelry, gold coins, diamonds and luxury watches. Evaluations are available without an obligation to sell. If you decide the final offer makes sense for you, same-day purchase and payment are available. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds 617 S. Hill Street Los Angeles, CA 90014 Phone: 310-663-1340 Visit Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds Frequently Asked Questions About Selling Gold Jewelry in Los Angeles What is the best place to sell gold jewelry in Los Angeles? For many sellers, an established local gold and jewelry buyer is a strong option because the jewelry can be weighed, tested and evaluated in person. Compare actual final offers and choose a buyer who clearly explains how the price was calculated. How is 14K gold jewelry valued? 14K gold is approximately 58.5% pure gold. Its starting metal value depends on the jewelry’s weight and the current gold price. The final purchase offer can also reflect refining costs, non-gold components, market conditions and whether the piece has additional resale value. Is 18K gold worth more than 14K gold? Per gram, 18K gold normally has more intrinsic gold value because it contains approximately 75% gold compared with about 58.5% for 14K gold. Can I sell broken gold jewelry? Yes. Broken chains, single earrings, damaged rings and other scrap gold can still contain significant precious-metal value even if the jewelry can no longer be worn. Can I sell gold without a receipt? A purchase receipt is generally not necessary simply to have gold jewelry evaluated, but legitimate secondhand dealers are required to verify seller identification. Bring valid government-issued photo identification. Should I clean my gold before selling it? Usually not. Cleaning does not change the amount of gold in the piece, and aggressive cleaning can potentially damage gemstones, finishes or collectible jewelry. Let the buyer evaluate the item in its current condition. Should I accept the highest phone quote? Not automatically. A preliminary quote made before a buyer verifies your jewelry may change after inspection. Compare the final dollar amount each buyer is actually prepared to pay after examining the item. Does a GIA report tell me how much my diamond is worth? No. A GIA Diamond Grading Report describes and grades the diamond’s characteristics. It does not assign a monetary appraisal or guarantee a resale price. Can designer jewelry be worth more than melt value? Yes. How Much Is My Gold Worth? The Complete 2026 Buyer Comparison

If you’re sitting on gold jewelry, coins, or luxury watches and asking “how much is my gold worth,” you’re not alone. Gold prices hit record highs in 2026, and market forecasts suggest continued strength through year-end. But determining the actual cash value of your items requires honest evaluation, current market data, and a buyer you can trust.

The truth is simple: your gold’s value depends on three factors—weight, purity, and the current spot price. But where you sell it matters just as much as what you’re selling. We’ve compared the top gold buyers in Los Angeles to help you understand fair market value and avoid underoffers.

What Your Gold Is Actually Worth: The Math

Let’s start with the numbers. As of 2026, here’s what pure gold and common alloys are trading at:

  • 24K gold (pure,.999+): $139.17 per gram
  • 18K gold (750 fineness): $104.38 per gram
  • 14K gold (585 fineness): $81.18 per gram
  • Current spot price basis: $4,328.64 per troy ounce

To calculate your own gold’s value, use this formula: Weight in troy ounces × Purity percentage × Spot price per troy ounce. Convert grams to troy ounces by dividing by 31.1. For example, if you have a 10-gram 14K gold ring, that’s 0.32 troy ounces × 0.585 purity × $4,328.64 = roughly $726 in melt value.

Most gold buyers won’t pay spot price—they’ll offer 70-85% of melt value after accounting for refining costs. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds typically offers 80-85% of melt value, which is significantly higher than industry average.

Why Timing Matters: Gold Price Trends in 2026

Gold prices are historically favorable right now. From May 2025 to May 2026, gold climbed 41%—from $3,335 per ounce to $4,732 per ounce. According to J.P. Morgan’s forecasts, gold is expected to average $6,000 per ounce by Q4 2026, potentially rising to $6,300 by the end of 2027.

If you’ve been holding onto inherited gold, broken jewelry, or unwanted watches, 2026 is one of the best times in years to convert them to cash. Market timing rarely favors sellers this clearly.

  • Expert, Transparent Evaluations: Their team has 19 years of experience buying gold, diamonds, watches, and estate jewelry. No pressure. No hidden fees. You see the scale, you see the calculation, you see the offer.
  • Same-Day Payment: Walk in, get evaluated, walk out with cash. No waiting, no checks, no mail delays.
  • Professional Environment: Located in Downtown Los Angeles with a pressure-free office. You’re treated like a valued client, not a transaction.
  • Buys Everything: Gold jewelry, diamond rings, Rolex watches, luxury watches, gold coins, estate jewelry, inherited collections. If it has value, they evaluate it.

Why Other Buyers Fall Short

Local Pawn Shops: Convenient, but their payouts typically hover at 60-70% of melt value. They’re lending businesses first, gold buyers second. You’ll leave with $250-$350 less than Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds would offer on the same ring.

National Gold Chains: They operate hundreds of locations and push volume over fair pricing. You’ll get slightly better than a pawn shop (65-75%), but still 10-15% below what you could get locally with a specialist.

Online Mail-In Services: They offer reasonable rates (70-78%), but you ship your valuables away, wait 5-7 days for payment, and have zero recourse if something goes wrong in transit. The peace of mind alone makes walking into a local buyer worth it.

Jewelry Store Trade-Ins: Forget it. Jewelry stores offer 50-65% because they mark up resale pieces 200-300%. Your gold subsidizes their inventory, not your pocket.

How to Maximize Your Gold’s Value Before You Sell

A few smart steps before you walk into any buyer:

  • Sort by Karat: 24K, 18K, and 14K gold are worth different amounts. Sorting them beforehand helps the evaluation go faster and shows you’re organized.
  • Weigh Everything: Use a kitchen scale to get a ballpark weight. It won’t be precise, but it helps you ballpark your own value and spot low offers.
  • Document Condition: Broken chains, missing stones, bent rings—none of it matters for melt value, but knowing what you have speeds up evaluation.
  • Bring Certificates: If you have certificates of authenticity for diamonds, gold coins, or luxury watches, bring them. They don’t change melt value for gold, but they matter for diamonds and collectible items.

Understanding Gold Fineness: What Karat Actually Means

Gold purity is measured in karats. Here’s what you need to know:

  • 24K: 99.9% pure gold (fineness.999). Soft, rarely used for jewelry, but highly valuable.
  • 22K: 91.7% pure gold (fineness.917). Common in Indian and Middle Eastern jewelry.
  • 18K: 75% pure gold (fineness.750). Popular for fine jewelry and watches. Most valuable for rings and necklaces.
  • 14K: 58.5% pure gold (fineness.585). Durable, affordable, most common in the U.S.
  • 10K: 41.7% pure gold (fineness.417). The legal minimum to be called “gold” in the U.S. Less valuable per gram.

If you’re not sure what karat your jewelry is, look for a stamp inside the band or on the clasp. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds‘s team can test any piece on the spot using acid testing and electronic analysis.

Real-World Example: What Your Gold Is Worth Right Now

Let’s walk through a real example. Say you have:

  • Three 14K gold rings totaling 15 grams
  • One 18K gold necklace weighing 8 grams
  • Total: 23 grams of mixed gold

Melt Value Calculation:

  • 15 grams 14K: 0.48 oz × 0.585 × $4,328.64 = $1,206
  • 8 grams 18K: 0.26 oz × 0.75 × $4,328.64 = $813
  • Total Melt Value: $2,019

What You’d Actually Get:

  • At Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds (85%): $1,716
  • At a National Chain (70%): $1,413
  • At a Pawn Shop (65%): $1,312
  • At a Jewelry Store (55%): $1,110

The Difference: Choosing Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds over a pawn shop nets you an extra $404 on this sale alone. On inherited collections or larger pieces, that difference easily reaches $1,000+.

Estate Jewelry, Inherited Gold, and Special Cases

If you’re liquidating an estate, inheritance, or divorce settlement, gold buying gets more nuanced. Some pieces have sentimental or antique value beyond melt price. Watches and diamonds need separate evaluation.

Related: Best Price for Diamonds in LA: Expert Guide 2026

This is where Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds‘s 19 years of experience shines. They evaluate not just gold weight, but whether your Rolex is a collectible model, whether your diamonds are high-quality, and whether your estate pieces have resale potential. You get offered fair melt value on everything, plus fair market value on anything with extra appeal.

Frequently Asked Questions

What’s the difference between spot price and what I’ll actually receive?

Spot price is what gold trades for on the commodities market—$4,328.64 per troy ounce as of 2026. But gold buyers can’t sell raw gold; they have to refine it, which costs money. Reputable buyers pass on 80-85% of the refining payout to you. Pawn shops and chains often keep 30-40%, offering you only 60-70%. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds’s rates are among the fairest because they specialize in precious metals and minimize overhead.

Should I wait for gold prices to go higher before I sell?

That’s personal, but consider this: J.P. Morgan forecasts suggest gold will average $6,000 per ounce by Q4 2026. Yes, prices could climb further in 2027. But timing the market is notoriously difficult, and you’re already looking at historically strong prices. If you need liquidity now, 2026 is genuinely favorable. If you’re holding inherited gold just in case, converting it to cash at today’s rates lets you invest elsewhere or use it immediately. Don’t let perfect be the enemy of good.

Do I need to clean or polish my gold before selling?

No. In fact, aggressive cleaning can scratch and damage pieces. Gold buyers assess weight and purity, not aesthetics. Bring your items as-is. If you have antique or vintage gold, leave the patina alone—it may indicate authenticity or age.

mainHtml:
When you walk in with a gold ring, necklace, or bracelet, the buyer doesn’t just glance at it and throw out a number. There’s a real process behind how jewelry buyers determine gold value, and understanding it helps you feel confident about the offer you get.

The truth is, gold value comes down to two primary factors: weight and purity. Everything else—the design, the brand, the condition—matters way less than these two things. Once a professional appraiser knows how much gold you actually have and how pure it is, they can calculate your offer in minutes.

Weight Is Step One: How Much Gold Do You Actually Have?

The first thing any jewelry buyer does is weigh your item. But here’s the thing—they’re not weighing the entire piece. They’re weighing just the gold.

If your ring has diamonds or gemstones, those get weighed separately. The buyer uses a precision scale to measure the gold-only weight, usually in grams. Sometimes older buyers still use pennyweights (1 pennyweight equals about 1.55 grams), but most modern shops work in grams now.

A 14K gold ring might weigh 5 grams total, but not all of that is pure gold. That’s where purity comes in.

Purity: Confirming What You Really Have

Your gold isn’t pure gold. Most gold jewelry is an alloy—meaning it’s mixed with other metals like copper, silver, or nickel. The purity mark tells you how much actual gold is in the piece.

You’ll see stamps like 10K, 14K, 18K, or 22K on your jewelry. These numbers represent the percentage of pure gold:

  • 10K gold = 41.7% pure gold
  • 14K gold = 58.3% pure gold
  • 18K gold = 75% pure gold
  • 22K gold = 91.7% pure gold

Professional buyers verify this purity using specialized tests. They might use an acid test, an electronic tester, or X-ray fluorescence (XRF) to confirm the stamp is accurate. Some pieces have no stamp at all—or the stamp is worn off—which is why independent verification matters.

If your 5-gram ring is stamped 14K, the buyer now knows it contains 2.92 grams of pure gold (5 grams × 58.3%). This is the number that actually determines your payout.

The Math: Converting Weight to Cash Value

Once the buyer knows the pure gold weight, they apply the current market price for gold. Gold is traded on global commodity markets, and the price changes daily. As of 2026, the price per gram fluctuates based on market conditions, economic factors, and supply and demand.

Here’s the simple math:

Pure gold weight (grams) × Current market price per gram = Raw gold value

If you have 2.92 grams of pure gold and the market price is $65 per gram, your raw gold value is about $190. But that’s not the final offer you’ll receive.

Reputable buyers like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds are transparent about how they calculate offers. Most buyers factor in a margin—they’re buying from you below spot price because they need to resell the gold and cover their operating costs. A fair offer is typically 70-90% of the raw gold value, depending on the buyer’s business model and current market conditions.

Explore Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds →

Market Rates: Why Price Varies by Day

Gold is a commodity, which means its price is set by global supply and demand, not by individual buyers. The London Bullion Market sets the standard gold price that most professional buyers reference.

This price changes constantly. Your gold ring might be worth $190 one day and $185 the next, just based on market movement. That’s why timing matters a little, but honestly—if you need cash today, the difference between today’s price and tomorrow’s is usually small.

Transparent buyers always tell you the current market rate they’re using and explain their margin. If a buyer can’t clearly explain how they got to their offer number, that’s a red flag.

What Doesn’t Determine Gold Value (But People Think It Does)

Here’s what doesn’t really matter when determining gold value:

  • The brand. A Cartier 14K gold bracelet and an unmarked 14K gold bracelet of the same weight and purity have the same gold value. (The brand matters for resale value if you’re selling the bracelet as jewelry, but if you’re selling for gold scrap, it’s irrelevant.)
  • The design or style. Whether your ring is vintage, modern, or has intricate details—the gold value is the same.
  • The condition. Scratched, dented, or broken gold is worth the same as pristine gold, weight for weight.
  • Diamonds or gemstones. These are valued separately based on the 4 Cs (cut, color, clarity, carat). They don’t affect the gold value calculation.

That said, some buyers specialize in estate jewelry and vintage pieces where the item’s overall value (beyond just gold) might be higher. But the gold-only appraisal process is always the same: weight and purity.

How Professional Buyers Stay Honest

When you’re choosing where to sell your gold, look for buyers who explain their process upfront. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds and other reputable buyers walk you through each step: weighing, purity testing, market rate calculation, and their margin.

A trustworthy buyer will:

  • Weigh your item in front of you
  • Show you the purity test results
  • Tell you the current market rate
  • Explain their calculation clearly
  • Give you an offer in writing before you decide
  • Never pressure you to sell on the spot

If a buyer rushes you, won’t show their work, or offers wildly different numbers than other buyers, keep shopping. The gold value doesn’t vary that much from buyer to buyer. If it does, someone’s being dishonest.

Estate and Inherited Jewelry: Same Process, Extra Value

If you inherited gold jewelry or you’re settling an estate, the gold value calculation is identical. The purity stamp and current market rate are what matter. However, some pieces might have collector value or historical significance beyond the gold itself. A professional appraisal can identify if your inherited piece is worth more as an heirloom than as scrap gold.

Why You Should Work With a Local, Transparent Buyer

Selling gold online or to mail-in services adds risk. You’re shipping your items and trusting that their scale is accurate and their offer is fair. In person, you can watch the entire process.

When you visit Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds in Downtown Los Angeles, you see the scale, you see the test results, and you get a same-day offer with no pressure. That transparency is worth the trip if you’re in the area.

What happens if my gold has no purity stamp?

A professional buyer will test it using acid, electronic, or XRF methods to determine the actual purity. Unmarked gold is more common than you’d think, especially with vintage or handmade pieces. The testing process takes just a few minutes and doesn’t damage your item.

Does the design or brand of my gold jewelry affect its value?

Not for gold-only value. A Tiffany ring and a generic ring of the same weight and karat will have the same gold value. However, if you’re selling to a buyer who specializes in designer jewelry, they might offer more for the brand itself. If you’re selling purely for gold, the brand is irrelevant.

How do I know if an offer is fair?

Get the numbers in writing. Ask the buyer to show you: the weight in grams, the purity percentage, the current market rate per gram, and the calculation they used. A fair offer is usually 70-85% of the raw gold value. If two buyers offer drastically different amounts, something’s off with one of them. Visit multiple buyers to compare.

Can I sell gold jewelry even if it’s broken or damaged?

Yes. The condition doesn’t matter for gold-only value. A bent, broken, or scratched ring is worth the same per gram as a pristine one. Damaged jewelry might have zero collector value, but its gold value is unchanged.

mainHtml:
Selling gold jewelry, diamonds, or luxury watches? The choice between a legitimate gold buyer and a pawn shop can cost you hundreds or even thousands of dollars. Here’s what you need to know before you walk through a door.

The Real Difference Between Legitimate Gold Buyers and Pawn Shops

At first glance, both seem to offer the same service: you bring in your gold, they evaluate it, and you walk out with cash. But the similarities end there.

Pawn shops are designed as short-term lending operations. Their primary business is loaning money against collateral, not buying precious metals outright. Gold buying is a side service, and speed is their priority, not fair valuation. Think of them as the convenience stores of gold buying.

Legitimate gold buyers, on the other hand, specialize in precious metals and jewelry. They invest in expertise, equipment, and market knowledge. Their reputation depends on fair pricing and transparency. Customers come back, refer friends, and leave honest reviews. That’s the business model.

Related: Best Jewelry District Gold Buyer in Los Angeles, CA

The result? Price differences between the best and worst gold offers can reach 50% for the same item. That’s not an exaggeration. A 10-gram gold ring could fetch $350 at one place and $700 at another.

Pricing: Where Pawn Shops Fall Short

Pawn shops typically pay less per gram for gold than specialized jewelry buyers. Why? They operate on thinner margins across thousands of product categories. They don’t have specialists evaluating your 14k wedding band or 18k gold chain. They have generalists running the operation.

Here’s what happens in a pawn shop:

  • They use basic scales and quick testing methods.
  • They apply a conservative discount to spot price because they need fast liquidity.
  • They factor in the cost of reselling your item, which adds overhead.
  • They assume you’ll take the first offer because you need money fast.

Legitimate gold buyers skip the middle steps. They have direct relationships with refiners, access to real-time spot prices, and the ability to hold inventory longer. That efficiency gets passed to you as a higher offer.

Transparency and Documentation

When you sell to Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, every step is documented. You see the scale reading. You understand the karat weight. You know the spot price and the dealer margin. It’s all written on your receipt.

Pawn shops? Many won’t break down the math. You get a number, take it or leave it. Some will refuse to tell you the spot price they’re using or explain their calculation. That opacity is a red flag.

Legitimate dealers also provide certificates of authenticity for gold bars and coins. If you’re selling inherited jewelry or estate items, documentation matters for your records and peace of mind.

Speed vs. Fair Price

Yes, pawn shops are fast. You can walk in and leave with cash in 15 minutes. But is speed worth losing $300 on a single transaction? Most sellers aren’t in such dire straits that they can’t spend 45 minutes getting a fair valuation.

Legitimate gold buyers prioritize fair pricing without sacrificing service. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, for example, offers same-day payment in a pressure-free environment. You’re not rushed. You’re treated with respect.

Price Per Gram Higher (competitive market) Lower (broad overhead)
Transparency Full breakdown on receipt Often vague or unclear
Expertise Specialized gemologists and evaluators Generalists across many categories
Documentation Certificates of authenticity available Basic receipt only
Payment Speed Same-day cash (no pressure) Immediate (convenience model)
Pressure to Sell Professional, pressure-free Often high (quick transaction model)
Reputation Impact Built on fair deals and repeat customers One-time transaction oriented

Why Legitimate Gold Buyers Win

Legitimate dealers like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds have been operating since 2007 because they’ve built trust through fair offers and expert evaluations. They know the gold market inside and out. They track spot prices in real time. They understand the difference between 10k, 14k, 18k, and 22k gold. They can spot genuine diamonds from cubic zirconia.

That expertise translates directly to your wallet. You’re not leaving money on the table because someone doesn’t know the true value of what you’re selling.

Additionally, legitimate buyers understand context. Are you selling inherited jewelry? Estate settlement? Downsizing your collection? They treat each situation with care and respect, not as a quick transaction.

How to Identify a Legitimate Gold Buyer

Not sure if you’re dealing with a real specialist or just another pawn operation? Look for these signs:

  • Physical location: A downtown storefront with professional display. No sketchy strip mall operations.
  • Years in business: Longevity matters. A 15+ year track record in gold buying is meaningful.
  • Online reputation: Check reviews on Google, Yelp, and local directories. Real testimonials from satisfied sellers.
  • Transparent pricing: They explain spot price, purity testing, and dealer margin before making an offer.
  • Specialized equipment: Professional scales, acid testing kits, magnification tools, ultrasonic cleaners.
  • Certifications: They provide documentation for valuable items like coins, bars, or certified diamonds.
  • No pressure: They let you walk away. They don’t rush you into a decision.

The Numbers Don’t Lie

Research consistently shows that reputable jewelers pay more for gold jewelry and scrap than pawn shops. According to industry data, the difference in per-gram rates for 10k gold alone can be 15-30% higher at specialized buyers.

That means if you’re selling $1,000 worth of gold, you could walk away with $850 at a pawn shop or $1,000+ at a legitimate buyer. It’s the difference between a fair deal and a discount.

If you’re in Los Angeles, Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds offers expert evaluations with transparent pricing. You can visit in person in Downtown LA, see the evaluation process, and leave with same-day payment. No obligation. No pressure.

Related: Best Gold Buyer Downtown Los Angeles | Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds

What About Mail-In Services?

Some online gold buyers offer mail-in programs. These can be legitimate alternatives to pawn shops, but they come with risks. You’re sending valuable items through the mail. You can’t see the evaluation process. You have to trust their appraisal.

The advantage is competitive pricing, often better than pawn shops. The disadvantage is lack of control and the time it takes. Local, in-person buyers let you maintain oversight throughout the process.

Related: White Gold vs Yellow Gold: Which Is Better for You?

The Bottom Line

Pawn shops serve a purpose for people in genuine emergencies who need immediate cash and can’t wait. But if you have even a few days, choosing a legitimate gold buyer is a no-brainer. You’ll get a fairer price, clearer documentation, and a professional experience without sales pressure.

Do yourself a favor: get multiple offers. Visit a specialized gold buyer. See the difference in valuations. Then decide. You might be surprised at how much more your gold is actually worth.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much more will I get selling to a legitimate buyer instead of a pawn shop?

The difference typically ranges from 15-50% depending on the item and current market conditions. On a $1,000 gold sale, you could expect $150-$500 more from a legitimate buyer. Get quotes from both to compare directly.

Is it safe to visit a gold buyer in person?

Yes. Reputable gold buyers operate professional, welcoming storefronts in established business districts. Bring a friend if you’d like. Legitimate dealers have nothing to hide and encourage transparency throughout the evaluation process.

What’s the difference between spot price and what I’ll actually get paid?

Spot price is the real-time market price for gold per ounce. Legitimate buyers subtract a dealer margin (typically 5-15% depending on purity and form) to account for refining, overhead, and profit. They should explain this calculation upfront. Pawn shops often use much wider margins without transparency.

Can I sell jewelry that’s damaged or incomplete?

Yes. Even broken, bent, or missing stones have value based on their gold content and weight. Legitimate buyers evaluate the precious metal content regardless of condition. Pawn shops may discount heavily for condition. This is another area where specialized buyers excel.
