Looking for the best price for diamonds in LA? Here’s the honest truth: you can save thousands by understanding how diamond pricing actually works, comparing your options, and knowing where to look. Whether you’re buying or selling, LA has some solid options, but you need to know what you’re doing to avoid overpaying or underselling.

Understanding Diamond Pricing in Los Angeles

Diamond prices vary wildly depending on where you shop. The Four Cs (cut, color, clarity, carat weight) matter, but so does the retailer’s markup and whether you’re buying natural or lab-grown diamonds.

Related: Diamond Price Guide 2026: What You’re Really Paying For

Related: How Much Should I Get for My Gold Jewelry? 2026 Guide

Related: Best Price for Diamonds in LA: Your Complete 2026 Guide

Related: Sell Inherited Jewelry No Obligation: Your Complete Guide

Here’s what most people don’t know: that old “three months’ salary” rule? It’s marketing garbage pushed by the diamond industry decades ago. Modern pricing is way more flexible, and you don’t need to follow that outdated standard anymore.

When you’re hunting for the best price for diamonds in LA, comparison shopping is your best friend. Check multiple retailers, look at online platforms with transparent pricing, and understand that local buyers often have different pricing structures than big-box chains.

Related: How Much Is My Gold Worth? 2026 Gold Buyer Comparison

Related: How Much Is My Gold Worth? 2026 Valuation Guide & Top Buyers Ranked

Lab-Grown Diamonds: The Best Value Option

If you want the absolute best price, lab-grown diamonds are your answer. They’re chemically identical to natural diamonds but cost significantly less—sometimes 30-40% cheaper for the same quality.

Lab diamonds are gaining serious traction in 2026. They’re becoming more accessible, easier to appraise, and more widely accepted. You can find high-quality lab diamond engagement rings starting around $3,000 at competitive LA retailers.

The catch? Not all jewelers embrace lab diamonds equally. Some still push natural stones because the markups are higher. That’s why working with transparent retailers matters. Look for shops that explain the difference without making you feel bad about choosing lab-grown.

Where to Find Competitive Pricing in LA

Los Angeles has some solid options for competitive diamond pricing. Here are the strategies that actually work:

  • Online comparison platforms: Sites like Rare Carat let you compare certified natural and lab-grown diamonds side by side. You can see pricing transparency before you ever visit a store.
  • Specialist retailers: Shops like Debebians are known for extremely competitive lab diamond pricing. They focus on value without sacrificing quality.
  • Local independent jewelers: Many LA independent jewelers offer custom pieces and bespoke services at competitive rates. You get personalized service plus fair pricing.

Don’t just walk into the first shop you see. Spend 30 minutes comparing prices online. The difference can be huge.

Are You Selling Diamonds in LA?

If you already own diamonds and want to sell, the strategy flips. You’re now looking for the best buyer who will pay fair market value without pressure or lowball offers.

This is where local expertise matters. A trusted local diamond buyer understands LA’s market, has relationships with certified appraisers, and can offer competitive prices on the spot.

When selling diamonds in LA, bring your paperwork—GIA certificates, appraisals, anything documenting the stone’s quality. Reputable buyers will evaluate your diamond independently and give you a transparent offer based on current market rates, not some arbitrary formula.

Same-day payment is standard at honest retailers. If a buyer is delaying payment or pushing you to decide immediately without time to think, walk out.

What Affects Diamond Prices in Los Angeles

Several factors shift pricing in LA specifically:

  • Local demand: LA’s luxury market is strong, which can affect both buying and selling prices.
  • Retailer overhead: Premium location shops (like those on Melrose Place, near 8483 Melrose Place, Los Angeles, CA 90069) have higher costs, which sometimes gets passed to customers.
  • Certification: GIA, AGS, or other certified diamonds command better prices and trust.
  • Market timing: Like any commodity, diamond prices fluctuate. Being aware of current market rates helps you negotiate better.

Pro tip: Don’t assume bigger always costs more. A well-cut 0.9-carat diamond can sometimes look larger and more brilliant than a poorly cut 1-carat stone—and cost less.

Explore Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds →

Custom and Bespoke Diamond Options

LA has a strong custom jewelry scene. If you’re looking for a one-of-a-kind piece, several jewelers specialize in bespoke engagement rings and custom diamond settings.

Related: How to Value Estate Jewelry Pieces: Expert Guide 2026

Related: Best Way to Sell Gold Jewelry in Los Angeles, CA | Expert Guide

Related: Loose Diamonds Appraised in Los Angeles – Expert Guide

Bespoke pieces can start at $8,900 and go way higher depending on the stone and design. The upside? You get exactly what you want. The downside? You’ll need patience and a clear budget conversation upfront.

When working with a custom jeweler for the best price for diamonds in LA, get everything in writing. Know the total cost before work starts. Reputable custom jewelers are transparent about timelines and costs—no surprises.

Red Flags to Avoid When Shopping for Diamonds

Not every seller in LA has your best interests in mind. Watch out for these warning signs:

  • Pressure to buy today with “limited-time” deals.
  • Refusal to show you certifications or appraisals.
  • Vague pricing or unwillingness to explain the Four Cs.
  • Claims that their diamonds are “better” without evidence.
  • Pushing you toward expensive stones without understanding your actual needs.

Honest jewelers explain everything, give you time to think, and back their claims with documentation. If something feels off, it probably is. Trust your gut and shop elsewhere.

How to Get a Fair Offer If You’re Selling

If you’re selling diamonds in LA—whether it’s estate jewelry, an inherited piece, or a stone you no longer want—getting a fair offer takes strategy.

Get your diamond independently appraised by a certified gemologist. Then approach multiple buyers. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds and other reputable local buyers will give you competitive offers without pressure. Compare them and choose the one that feels right.

Don’t accept the first offer if it feels low. Honest buyers expect you to shop around. They’ll match competitive offers if your stone is solid because they know they’re getting quality merchandise.

Same-day payment, no haggling, professional evaluations—these are baseline expectations at legitimate diamond buyers in LA. Anything less, keep looking.

Key Takeaways for Getting the Best Price

Whether you’re buying or selling diamonds in LA, the fundamentals are the same: get educated, compare options, and work with honest professionals who value transparency.

Lab-grown diamonds offer the best value if you’re buying. Natural diamonds still command higher prices but aren’t always worth the premium. Online comparison tools make price shopping easier than ever.

If you’re selling, expect fair market value based on current pricing, not inflated retail markups. Certified appraisals, professional evaluation, and same-day payment from a trusted buyer should be non-negotiable. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds has been a Downtown LA staple since 2007 for exactly this reason—transparency, fair offers, and immediate payment without pressure.

FAQs About Diamond Prices in LA

What’s a fair price for a 1-carat diamond in LA right now?

It depends on quality and whether it’s natural or lab-grown. A high-quality natural 1-carat diamond typically ranges from $3,500 to $8,000+ depending on the Four Cs. Lab-grown 1-carat diamonds cost significantly less, usually $1,500 to $3,500. Always check current pricing on platforms like Rare Carat for transparent market rates.

Should I buy diamonds online or in person in LA?

Both have advantages. Online gives you transparent pricing and easy comparisons. In-person lets you see the stone and build a relationship with a jeweler. For peace of mind, many people research online then visit a trusted local buyer like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds to inspect and finalize the deal.

How do I know if I’m getting a fair price when selling my diamonds?

Get an independent appraisal from a certified gemologist first. Then get offers from multiple buyers. Legitimate diamond buyers will evaluate your stone professionally and offer fair market value without pressure. Same-day payment and professional evaluations are standard at reputable shops.

Are lab-grown diamonds a good investment?

Lab-grown diamonds hold value reasonably well but don’t appreciate like natural diamonds. They’re best if you want the look and durability of a diamond at a lower price point. If investment potential matters, natural stones are traditionally the safer bet, though you’ll pay more upfront.

mainHtml:
You’ve decided it’s time to sell that gold jewelry sitting in your drawer. Smart move. But here’s the thing: not all buyers pay the same, and the difference between a fair offer and a lowball can be hundreds of dollars. The good news? You don’t need to guess. This guide walks you through exactly how to sell gold jewelry and get maximum value in the Los Angeles area, from Downtown LA to Long Beach, Pasadena, and beyond.

Why Selling Gold Jewelry Matters Right Now

Gold prices are dynamic, and timing can work in your favor. Whether you’re dealing with inherited jewelry, estate items, or pieces you simply don’t wear anymore, selling gold jewelry is straightforward when you know what to expect.

Related: Sell Gold Jewelry Downtown Los Angeles: Best Buyers & Prices

Related: Sell Inherited Jewelry No Obligation: Your Complete Guide

Here’s what most people don’t realize: pawn shops typically offer only about 30% of spot value. Coin shops do better at 80-85%. But the real advantage? Working with a specialist buyer who understands the full value of your pieces. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds has been buying gold jewelry across the Los Angeles area since 2007, and we know exactly what fair market value looks like.

Related: Best Jewelry District Gold Buyer in Los Angeles, CA

Step 1: Get Your Gold Professionally Appraised

Before you approach any buyer, you need to know what you’re selling. Professional authentication and appraisal are critical. This isn’t optional; it’s your foundation for negotiating confidently.

Here’s what a real appraisal includes:

  • Accurate karat weight (10K, 14K, 18K, etc.)
  • Total gram weight of the gold content
  • Condition and any gemstones attached
  • Current market value based on live gold prices

You’ll want to sort your jewelry by karat weight too. That 14K necklace won’t be valued the same as a 10K ring. Understanding this breakdown helps you ask smarter questions when you’re ready to sell. Learn exactly how 14K gold necklaces are valued to get a real sense of the numbers.

Step 2: Know Current Gold Prices

Gold prices fluctuate daily. Before you sell, check what spot gold is trading at. According to recent data from the Kitco Gold Price Index, you can track live prices in real time.

Why does this matter? A buyer might quote you a percentage of spot value. If you don’t know spot, you won’t know if the offer is fair. Arm yourself with that information before you walk in.

Pro tip: Compare quotes from at least three different buyers on the same day. Gold prices move, so comparing on the same day ensures you’re looking at apples to apples.

Step 3: Choose Your Buyer Type

You have options for where to sell gold jewelry. Each has tradeoffs:

  • Local jewelry stores: May offer convenience, but their buyback rates vary wildly.
  • Pawn shops: Fast, but notorious for low offers (often 30% of spot).
  • Coin and metal dealers: Better rates (80-85% of spot), but may focus on coins rather than jewelry.
  • Specialized precious metals buyers: Often offer the most competitive rates and treat fine jewelry with care.

The reality: if you want professional treatment, transparent pricing, and fair market value in a pressure-free environment, specialized buyers serve you better. Compare local versus online gold buyers to see which approach works for your situation.

What to Bring When You Sell Gold Jewelry

Get organized before you walk in. Bring:

  • All pieces you’re selling (separated by karat weight if possible)
  • Your appraisal documentation
  • Any original receipts or certificates
  • A valid ID
  • A list of current spot gold prices

Don’t let anyone pressure you into selling on the spot. A reputable buyer will answer your questions, show you the scale, explain their calculations, and let you think it over if you need to.

Why Location Matters: Selling in the Los Angeles Area

If you’re in Los Angeles, Long Beach, Santa Monica, Pasadena, Glendale, or anywhere within 50 miles of Downtown LA, you have access to established local buyers who understand the regional market. This is your advantage. You don’t have to mail anything off or wait weeks for payment.

Explore Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds →

Local buyers can:

  • Examine your pieces in person
  • Offer same-day payment in cash
  • Handle inherited and estate jewelry with care and respect
  • Provide transparent explanations of their offer

If you’re selling estate or inherited jewelry in Los Angeles, working with a local specialist means you get fair value plus the peace of mind that comes with a trusted, established business.

Related: How to Value Estate Jewelry Pieces: Expert Guide 2026

Common Reasons People Sell Gold Jewelry

Your reason for selling doesn’t matter to the buyer. What matters is getting fair value. But it helps to know you’re in good company:

  • Estate settlements: Liquidating inherited items to settle estates.
  • Divorce-related sales: Dividing assets and starting fresh.
  • Financial needs: Converting unused assets to cash quickly.
  • Downsizing collections: Simplifying and clearing space.
  • Upgrading jewelry: Trading older pieces for something you’ll actually wear.

Whatever your reason, the process is the same: get appraised, compare offers, and sell to a buyer you trust.

Red Flags to Avoid When Selling Gold Jewelry

Protect yourself. Watch out for these warning signs:

  • Buyers who won’t show you the scale or explain their calculations
  • Pressure to sell immediately without time to think
  • Refusal to provide a written offer
  • Appraisers working on commission (conflict of interest)
  • Offers that seem too good to be true (they usually are)

A legitimate buyer will welcome your questions and give you time. They understand you’re making a financial decision, and they respect that.

Maximize Your Gold Jewelry Sale

You can do a few things to get the best outcome:

  • Sell when gold prices are trending upward, not during dips
  • Clean your jewelry gently before showing it (but don’t overdo it)
  • Keep all documentation and certificates
  • Compare at least three offers before deciding
  • Ask about any fees or deductions upfront

The goal is informed confidence. You walk in knowing your item’s value, you hear the buyer’s offer, and you make a decision without pressure.

Next Steps: Sell Your Gold Jewelry Today

Ready to turn that gold into cash? The best time to start is now. Visit Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds in Downtown Los Angeles. We’ve been serving the Los Angeles area and surrounding communities for nearly two decades. We handle gold jewelry, diamonds, luxury watches, estate pieces, and inherited valuables with professionalism and respect.

What you get:

  • Expert evaluation of every piece
  • Transparent, competitive offers based on current market rates
  • Same-day payment in cash
  • A pressure-free environment where you feel heard

Stop wondering. Get a real quote today.

How much will my gold jewelry sell for?

That depends on the karat weight, total gram weight, current spot price, and any gemstones. A professional appraisal gives you the exact number. As a general example, a 14K gold necklace weighing 10 grams might be worth $300 to $400 depending on current gold prices, but every piece is unique.

Can I sell gold jewelry with gemstones attached?

Absolutely. Buyers will evaluate the gold content and the gemstones separately. Diamonds, sapphires, rubies, and other stones add value. Make sure the appraiser examines the stones carefully so you get credit for them.

Do I need to bring anything special when I sell my gold jewelry?

Bring your pieces, a valid ID, and any documentation you have (original receipts, certificates, appraisals). A list of current gold prices is helpful too, so you can verify the offer against market rates.

How long does the process take?

From appraisal to payment, expect 30 to 45 minutes with a reputable buyer. They’ll examine your items, explain their valuation, make an offer, and if you accept, pay you on the spot. No waiting, no mailing, no complications.

If you have a 10K gold ring, chain, bracelet, necklace, or broken jewelry sitting at home, one of the first questions you may ask is: How much is 10K gold worth per gram at a pawn shop?

There isn’t one fixed answer.

The 10K gold price per gram is subject to market fluctuations, so it’s essential to stay updated.

When estimating the 10K gold price per gram, remember that the purity affects the overall worth.

The 10K gold price per gram changes with the current gold market, and the amount a pawn shop or gold buyer offers can also depend on the weight of your jewelry, its actual purity, whether it contains stones or non-gold components, and whether the piece has additional resale value.

The 10K gold price per gram can vary based on the buyer’s evaluation standards.

The most important thing to understand before selling is that 10K gold is approximately 41.7% pure gold. That means the value of 10K jewelry can be estimated from the current price of pure gold, but the calculated gold value and the cash offer you receive are not necessarily the same amount.

If you’re considering selling your jewelry in Los Angeles, understanding this calculation can help you compare offers and make a more informed decision.

How Is the 10K Gold Price Per Gram Calculated?

The starting point for determining the value of 10K gold is the current spot price of gold.

Gold is normally quoted internationally by the troy ounce, and one troy ounce equals approximately 31.1035 grams.

Because 24K gold is considered essentially pure gold and 10K gold contains 10 parts gold out of 24, the theoretical purity of 10K gold is:

10 ÷ 24 = 41.67%

For accurate evaluations, reference the 10K gold price per gram.

So a simple estimate of the intrinsic gold value of 10K jewelry is:The 10K gold price per gram can serve as a reference point for negotiations.Understanding the 10K gold price per gram can maximize your selling potential.

Researching the 10K gold price per gram will empower your selling strategy.

Current pure gold price per gram × 41.67% = approximate 10K gold value per gram

For example, if pure gold were worth $100 per gram, the theoretical gold content of one gram of 10K gold would be worth approximately:

A buyer will consider the 10K gold price per gram when making an offer for your jewelry.

The 10K gold price per gram does not always reflect what pawn shops will pay.

$100 × 0.4167 = $41.67

Always check the latest 10K gold price per gram before visiting a buyer.

Often, the 10K gold price per gram will guide your expectations during transactions.

This is only an example—not today’s gold price or a guaranteed purchase price.

You can check the current market price through an established precious-metals market source such as GoldPrice.org before getting your jewelry evaluated.

How Much Do Pawn Shops Pay Per Gram for 10K Gold?

A pawn shop’s offer for 10K gold is generally not the same as the theoretical value of the pure gold contained in the jewelry.

A business purchasing gold needs to account for testing, processing, refining, market movement, overhead, and its own operating margin. Different businesses can therefore make different offers for the exact same piece.

This is why we do not recommend relying on a universal claim such as “pawn shops always pay 40% to 60% of gold value.”

There is no single percentage that applies to every pawn shop, every gold buyer, or every transaction.

Instead, when comparing offers, ask:

  • What karat did you test my jewelry at?
  • What is the total payable gold weight?
  • What gold market price are you using?
  • How was my offer calculated?
  • Are stones or other non-gold components being deducted from the weight?
  • Does the piece have resale, designer, collectible, or gemstone value beyond its melt value?

Knowing the answers gives you a much better basis for comparing buyers.

Why Is 10K Gold Worth Less Than 14K or 18K Gold?

The difference comes primarily from gold purity.

The most common gold purities used in jewelry include:

If two pieces have exactly the same weight, the higher-karat piece generally contains more pure gold and therefore has a higher intrinsic gold value.

For example, a 10-gram 10K chain contains approximately 4.17 grams of theoretical pure gold content, while a 10-gram 14K chain contains approximately 5.83 grams.

However, purity and weight aren’t always the entire story.

What Determines How Much Your 10K Gold Jewelry Is Worth?

When a professional buyer evaluates gold jewelry, several factors can affect its potential value.

1. Gold Purity

The first question is whether the piece is actually 10K.

Jewelry may be stamped 10K, 10KT, or 417, but markings alone should not always be relied upon. A buyer can test the item to verify its purity.

2. Weight

Gold jewelry is commonly weighed in grams.

The heavier the actual gold content of your piece, the greater its intrinsic metal value, assuming the same purity.

However, the gross weight of a piece isn’t necessarily all gold. Gemstones, watch movements, clasps, springs, steel components, and other materials may need to be considered separately.

3. Current Gold Spot Price

Gold prices fluctuate throughout the trading day.

That means an article giving you a fixed price such as “$20 per gram” can quickly become outdated.

A better approach is to understand the formula and check the current market before you sell.

4. Diamonds and Gemstones

If your 10K gold jewelry contains diamonds or other potentially valuable stones, the piece should not automatically be treated as nothing more than scrap gold.

The stones may have value separate from the gold.

This is especially important for diamond rings, estate jewelry, and higher-quality pieces.

5. Brand and Resale Value

Some jewelry can be worth more intact than its metal content alone.

Designer jewelry, collectible pieces, certain antique items, and desirable estate jewelry may deserve additional evaluation before being treated strictly as scrap.

That’s one reason choosing an experienced jewelry buyer can matter.

10K Gold Value Example

Here’s a simple hypothetical example.

Suppose you have a 10-gram 10K gold chain.

Because 10K gold is approximately 41.67% pure:

10 grams × 0.4167 = approximately 4.167 grams of pure gold content

Next, multiply that number by the current market price of pure gold per gram.

If pure gold were hypothetically trading at $100 per gram:

4.167 × $100 = $416.70

In this hypothetical example, approximately $416.70 represents the theoretical value of the contained gold before considering the buyer’s costs, margin, refining, deductions, or any additional resale value.

It does not mean a pawn shop or gold buyer will pay exactly $416.70.

That’s an important distinction when you’re researching how much 10K gold is worth.

Is 10K Gold Considered Scrap Gold?

It can be.

“Scrap gold” generally refers to gold being valued primarily for its precious-metal content rather than as a finished piece of jewelry.

Examples can include:

  • Broken gold chains
  • Bent rings
  • Single earrings
  • Damaged bracelets
  • Old or unwanted jewelry
  • Jewelry missing stones
  • Pieces that are difficult to resell intact

The good news is that broken gold can still have significant precious-metal value.

A broken 10K chain doesn’t suddenly stop containing gold because the clasp is damaged.

If you have broken or unwanted jewelry, our guide to selling gold jewelry in Downtown Los Angeles explains what to expect during an in-person evaluation.

Pawn Shop vs. Gold Buyer: Where Should You Sell 10K Gold?

Pawn shops and dedicated gold buyers operate differently.

A pawn shop may provide both collateral loans and outright purchases. If you pawn an item, you’re borrowing money against it and can generally reclaim it by repaying the loan according to the agreement.

Selling is different: ownership transfers to the buyer.

Understanding the 10K gold price per gram will help you when deciding between a pawn shop or a gold buyer.

A specialized gold and jewelry buyer generally focuses on evaluating and purchasing precious metals, jewelry, diamonds, coins, watches, and related valuables.

Neither business type should automatically be assumed to offer the highest price.

Instead, compare the actual offers.

If you’re researching your options locally, see our guide to choosing a gold buyer in Downtown Los Angeles.

How to Get the Best Price for Your 10K Gold

There are several things you can do before accepting an offer.

Check the Gold Market

Know approximately where gold is trading before visiting a buyer.

You don’t need to become a commodities expert. You simply want a reference point for understanding your jewelry’s underlying gold content.

Know the Karat

Look for markings such as 10K or 417.

A marking isn’t a substitute for professional testing, but it gives you a starting point.

Know the Weight

If possible, know approximately how many grams your jewelry weighs.

Remember that gemstones and non-gold components can affect the payable gold weight.

Get an In-Person Evaluation

Photographs can help identify an item, but an accurate purchase offer may require inspecting and testing the actual jewelry.

At an in-person evaluation, you can also ask questions about the weight, purity, stones, and how the offer was determined.

Compare Offers

You don’t have to accept the first offer you receive.

If you’re uncertain about the value of your jewelry, comparing offers from established buyers can help you understand the market.

Don’t Assume Everything Should Be Melted

Before selling designer, antique, estate, diamond, or collectible jewelry strictly for its gold content, find out whether the complete piece has additional value.

For a broader explanation of the selling process, read our guide to selling gold jewelry in Los Angeles.

Can You Sell 10K Gold Without a Receipt?

In many situations, the original retail receipt isn’t what determines the gold value of the item.

A professional buyer can examine the jewelry, test its purity, weigh it, and evaluate other relevant characteristics.

However, sellers should be prepared to comply with any identification or transaction requirements that apply to the buyer and transaction.

If you have original paperwork for designer jewelry, diamonds, or other valuable pieces, bring it with you because documentation can sometimes help establish what you have.

Does Cleaning 10K Gold Increase Its Value?

Cleaning ordinary scrap gold generally does not increase the amount of pure gold contained in the piece.

A 10-gram 10K item doesn’t become more valuable as gold simply because it is shinier.

More importantly, aggressive polishing or improper chemical cleaning can potentially damage certain jewelry, gemstones, finishes, or collectible pieces.

If you’re unsure, leave the jewelry as it is and let the buyer evaluate it.

Does a 10K Gold Stamp Guarantee the Jewelry Is Real?

No marking should be treated as an absolute guarantee by itself.

Stamps can be misleading, altered, or counterfeit.

A professional evaluation may use appropriate testing methods to determine whether the piece is gold and estimate its purity.

Common markings associated with 10K gold include:

10K, 10KT and 417

The number 417 refers to approximately 41.7% gold content.

What If My 10K Gold Jewelry Contains Diamonds?

This is where choosing the right buyer becomes especially important.

Suppose you have a 10K diamond ring. There may be at least two components to evaluate:

The gold setting and the diamond or diamonds.

If the stones have meaningful market value, you want a buyer capable of evaluating them rather than automatically calculating an offer based only on the gold weight.

The same principle applies to estate and designer jewelry.

There is no universal pawn-shop price for 10K gold. Offers can vary by buyer and transaction. Instead of relying on a fixed percentage, ask how the buyer determined the weight, purity, gold price, deductions, and final offer.

If you’re searching for a Rolex buyer in Los Angeles who pays cash, you’re in the right place. Selling a luxury watch doesn’t have to be complicated or stressful. The truth is, Rolex watches hold their value like few other items do, and there are trusted local buyers in LA ready to evaluate yours and pay you on the spot.

Whether you inherited a vintage Rolex, you’re upgrading your collection, going through a life change, or just need quick cash, selling to a local expert beats shipping your watch to some stranger online. Let’s walk through exactly how to find the right buyer and get the most money for your timepiece.

Related: How to Sell a Rolex Watch in Los Angeles: Cash Today

Related: How Much Is My Gold Worth? 2026 Gold Buyer Comparison

Related: GIA Certified Diamonds 2026: Top Buyers & Best Places to Sell

Why Sell Your Rolex Locally in Los Angeles

Los Angeles has a huge market for luxury watches. That means competition between buyers, which is good for you because it keeps offers honest and fair.

Related: Best Places to Sell a Rolex Watch in Los Angeles

Related: Diamond: What It Is, How to Value It & Where to Sell

When you sell locally, you get immediate payment. No waiting weeks for a wire transfer or check to arrive. You walk in, your watch gets evaluated by someone who actually knows Rolex watches inside and out, you get an offer, and if you accept, you leave with cash the same day.

You also get to see the buyer’s operation in person. You can ask questions, understand exactly what they’re looking for, and feel confident about the transaction before it happens. That peace of mind is worth a lot.

What Makes a Good Rolex Buyer

Not all watch buyers are the same. A good Rolex buyer in Los Angeles should check a few boxes.

First, they need expertise. Rolex makes thousands of models across decades, and prices vary wildly based on condition, rarity, age, and whether the original paperwork is included. A buyer who knows the difference between a 1976 Rolex Oyster Perpetual Datejust and a 2015 model will give you an accurate appraisal. If a buyer seems to offer the same price for every Rolex that walks through the door, move on.

Second, transparency matters. You should understand exactly why they’re offering what they’re offering. What condition is your watch in? Are they counting the original box and papers? Is the movement original? A trustworthy buyer explains their reasoning without being pushy.

Third, same-day payment is non-negotiable. If a buyer wants to “check with their boss” or “verify something” and asks you to come back, that’s a red flag. Legitimate Rolex buyers like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds have the authority and cash on hand to pay immediately after evaluation.

How to Get the Most Money for Your Rolex

Before you walk into any buyer’s office, do a few things to maximize your offer.

Clean your watch gently. Use a soft cloth and warm water. Don’t take it apart or try to polish the case yourself. Buyers actually prefer to see watches in their genuine, unrestored condition because that’s easier to appraise accurately.

Find your original paperwork and box. If you have the original Rolex box, warranty card, or service documentation, bring it. This can add real money to your offer. A Rolex with papers is worth noticeably more than the same watch without them.

Know roughly what year your Rolex is. You can usually find this on the Rolex website or by looking at the serial number. Knowing whether you have a vintage, pre-owned, or recent model helps the buyer move faster and gives you confidence in their appraisal.

Have realistic expectations. Rolex watches hold value well, but they don’t appreciate forever. A used Rolex typically sells for 50-70% of its original retail price, depending on age, condition, and demand. If you paid $8,000 for a watch five years ago, don’t expect $10,000. But a fair buyer will offer you something close to current market value.

Finding a Trusted Rolex Buyer Near You

Los Angeles has several options if you search online, but not all are equally reliable. Some are pawn shops (avoid these if you want fair pricing). Some are online-only resellers who don’t buy direct from customers.

The best approach: look for a established local jewelry and watch buyer with a physical location downtown or in your neighborhood. Check their reviews on Google. Look for mentions of fair offers, same-day payment, and professional staff. If you see reviews saying “I felt rushed” or “their offer was way low,” keep looking.

A few quick ways to vet a buyer:

  • Call ahead with basic details about your watch (model, approximate year, condition). If they ask thoughtful questions, that’s good.
  • Visit in person before you commit to selling. See how they treat you and your watch. Do they handle it carefully? Do they explain things clearly?
  • Ask how long they’ve been buying Rolex watches. Someone with years of experience is safer than a startup.

When you’re ready to sell, Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds is a downtown Los Angeles-based buyer with over 15 years of experience evaluating and purchasing luxury watches like Rolex. They handle vintage and modern models, pay same-day, and pride themselves on transparent appraisals with no pressure.

Related: Best Gold Buyer Downtown Los Angeles | Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds

What Affects Your Rolex’s Cash Value

Several factors influence what a buyer will pay for your specific Rolex.

Model and rarity. Some Rolex models are highly sought after (like the Submariner or GMT-Master II). Others are less common. Rarity usually means higher value.

Age. Vintage Rolex watches (1970s-1990s) are very popular right now. They often sell for strong prices because collectors love the history. Newer Rolex watches (2000s-present) are common and valued closer to retail.

Condition. Is the dial original or has it been refinished? Are there scratches on the case? Does the movement still run accurately? Condition dramatically affects price. A pristine vintage Rolex can be worth triple a heavily worn one.

Papers and boxes. Original documentation and the original Rolex box add significant value. A watch with everything intact is worth more than the same watch without.

Movement type. Is it automatic or manual wind? Some collectors prefer one over the other, which affects demand and price.

The Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds Difference

When you’re selling something valuable, trust matters. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds has been buying gold, diamonds, and luxury watches in Los Angeles since 2007. That’s nearly two decades of evaluating watches like yours, developing relationships with collectors, and understanding fair market prices.

Their approach is straightforward: they evaluate your Rolex carefully, explain the appraisal, make a fair cash offer, and if you’re happy, you get paid the same day. No high-pressure sales tactics. No ridiculous lowball offers. Just honest business.

They understand that selling inherited jewelry, downsizing a collection, or dealing with an estate settlement is often personal. That’s why they focus on making the process respectful and transparent. You’re not just selling a watch. You’re trusting someone with something that has history and meaning.

Related: Sell Inherited Jewelry No Obligation: Your Complete Guide

Next Steps: Selling Your Rolex for Cash

Ready to sell? Here’s what to do next.

Step 1: Gather what you have. Find your Rolex, the box (if you kept it), any paperwork, and give it a gentle clean.

Step 2: Get a quick phone appraisal. Call a few local buyers and describe your watch. You don’t need to know the exact model number right away. Just tell them what you know (approximate year, condition, whether you have papers). This gives you a ballpark before you visit.

Step 3: Visit in person. Schedule an appointment if possible. Bring your watch and any documentation. Let the buyer examine it thoroughly.

Step 4: Listen to the appraisal. Ask questions. Understand the offer. A reputable buyer like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds will explain their reasoning clearly and answer anything you ask.

Step 5: Decide. You’re never obligated to sell on the spot. Take your time. If the offer feels right and the buyer feels trustworthy, accept it and get your cash.

How much cash can I expect for my Rolex?

It depends entirely on the model, age, condition, and current market demand. A used Rolex typically sells for 50-70% of its original retail price. A vintage Rolex from the 1970s-80s might sell for more if it’s rare and well-maintained. A recent Rolex in excellent condition might fetch 60-75% of what it cost new. The only way to know for sure is to get a professional appraisal. Contact Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds for a free evaluation.

Do I need the original box and papers to sell my Rolex?

No, but they help. A Rolex with original documentation and packaging is worth more than the same watch without. If you don’t have them, don’t worry—your watch still has value. Just be prepared for the offer to reflect that absence.

Can I sell a Rolex that’s not working?

Yes. Even if the movement has stopped, a Rolex has value. Buyers purchase non-working watches for parts or to have them serviced and resold. You’ll get less than a fully functional watch, but it’s still worth something. A professional buyer will evaluate it honestly and let you know.

How long does the selling process take?

If you visit a local buyer like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, the evaluation usually takes 15-30 minutes. They’ll examine the watch, check its movement, verify authenticity, and make an offer. If you accept, you can have cash the same day. The whole process from walking in to leaving with payment is often under an hour.

If you own a 14K gold ring, bracelet, necklace, chain, earrings, broken jewelry, or inherited gold, one of the first questions you may ask is: “How much is my 14K gold worth?”

The answer starts with the 14K gold price per gram, but the market price of gold is only part of the calculation.

To understand the 14K gold price per gram, it’s essential to consider recent trends and fluctuations in the market.

The weight of your jewelry, its actual gold purity, the current gold market, gemstones, brand or resale value, and the buyer evaluating the piece can all affect the amount you ultimately receive.

For Los Angeles sellers, understanding these factors before visiting a gold buyer can make it much easier to compare offers and recognize a fair evaluation. If you want a broader explanation covering different karats and types of jewelry, read our complete guide to understanding how much your gold is worth.

What Is 14K Gold?

14K gold contains approximately 58.3% pure gold. The remaining portion consists of other metals that help provide durability, color, and strength.

The term “14 karat” means that 14 of 24 parts of the alloy are gold. The Gemological Institute of America (GIA) provides additional technical information about determining the gold content of jewelry metals.

You may see 14K jewelry stamped with markings such as:

  • 14K
  • 14KT
  • 583
  • 585

The exact marking can vary depending on where and when the jewelry was manufactured.

Because 14K gold combines substantial gold content with greater durability than higher-purity gold, it is commonly used for rings, chains, bracelets, earrings, pendants, and other everyday jewelry.

For additional information about the market for this particular purity, see our 14 Karat Gold Market 2026 statistics and pricing report.

What Is the 14K Gold Price Per Gram?

There is no single permanent 14K gold price per gram because the underlying price of pure gold changes with the market.

A useful way to estimate the theoretical gold content is:

Pure gold price per gram × 58.3% = approximate 14K gold melt value per gram

Gold is commonly quoted internationally by the troy ounce. According to the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), one troy ounce is approximately 31.1035 grams.

Every seller wants the best value based on the 14K gold price per gram.

Therefore, when gold is quoted by the troy ounce:

Gold spot price per troy ounce ÷ 31.1035 = approximate pure gold price per gram

Then:

Pure gold price per gram × 0.583 = approximate 14K gold value per gram

This calculation estimates the underlying precious-metal value. It does not automatically mean that a gold buyer will pay that exact amount.

Example: How to Calculate the Value of 14K Gold

Suppose you have a 14K gold bracelet that weighs 25 grams.

First, determine approximately how much pure gold it contains:

25 grams × 0.583 = approximately 14.58 grams of pure gold

You can then multiply the estimated pure-gold content by the current pure gold price per gram:

25 grams × 0.583 × current pure gold price per gram = estimated melt value

Using a formula instead of placing a fixed gold price in this article keeps the calculation useful even when the market changes.

Remember that this represents an estimated underlying metal value—not necessarily the final cash offer.

How Much Is 14K Gold Worth Today?

The value of 14K gold changes as the gold market moves.

If the spot price of gold rises, the underlying melt value of 14K jewelry generally rises as well. If the spot price falls, its melt value generally declines.

However, two pieces of 14K jewelry with the same weight do not necessarily have the same total resale value.

A professional evaluation may also consider:

  • Exact weight
  • Verified gold purity
  • Diamonds or gemstones
  • Designer or luxury brand
  • Condition
  • Craftsmanship
  • Collectibility
  • Potential resale value
  • Current market demand

This is why simply searching “14K gold price today” cannot always tell you exactly what a particular piece of jewelry is worth.

Does 14K Yellow, White, or Rose Gold Have the Same Gold Value?

If each item is genuinely the same karat purity and weight, 14K yellow gold, 14K white gold, and 14K rose gold contain approximately the same proportion of pure gold.

The different colors primarily come from the metals alloyed with the gold.

Therefore, when jewelry is valued primarily for its gold content, color by itself usually does not create a major difference in the underlying gold value.

However, a particular piece may still be worth more because of its brand, design, gemstones, condition, age, or resale demand.

Why the Weight of Your 14K Gold Matters

Gold buyers commonly evaluate precious metals using grams, pennyweights, or troy ounces.

One troy ounce equals approximately 31.1035 grams.

If you are comparing offers, make sure you understand which unit of measurement each buyer is using.

A price quoted “per gram” cannot be directly compared with a price quoted “per pennyweight” without converting the units.

You should also ask whether stones or other non-gold components are included in the displayed weight and how those components affect the calculation.

Why a 14K Stamp Is Not the Entire Evaluation

A 14K or 585 stamp is useful evidence, but a professional gold buyer may still test the jewelry.

Stamps can wear down, jewelry can be repaired with different metals, and some pieces may contain multiple components with different purity levels.

Depending on the item, a professional evaluation may include:

  • Visual inspection
  • Hallmark examination
  • Accurate weighing
  • Acid testing
  • Electronic testing
  • XRF analysis when appropriate

Testing helps determine what is actually being purchased rather than relying only on a stamp.

Melt Value vs. What a Gold Buyer Pays

One of the most important concepts for gold sellers is the difference between melt value and a buyer’s actual offer.

Melt value represents the theoretical value of the pure gold contained in the item based on the current market price.

A buyer’s offer may be lower because a gold-buying business has costs associated with testing, processing, refining, market risk, overhead, and profit.

On the other hand, some jewelry can be worth more than its basic melt value.

A desirable designer bracelet, luxury-brand piece, antique item, collectible jewelry, or jewelry containing valuable diamonds may deserve an evaluation beyond its gold content alone.

That is why automatically selling every piece strictly as scrap gold can sometimes leave money on the table.

Our guide to how much you should get for gold jewelry explains the difference between underlying gold value and an actual purchase offer in greater detail.

Highest Quote vs. Final Offer: Know the Difference

When comparing gold buyers, don’t evaluate a buyer only by the highest price quoted over the phone or advertised online.

The highest initial quote is not necessarily the highest amount you will actually receive.

Some buyers may provide an unusually attractive preliminary estimate based on assumptions about weight, purity, condition, or market value. After the item is examined in person, the final offer may be substantially different.

A very high initial number can also anchor a seller’s expectations. If competing buyers cannot match that quoted figure, the seller may return to the original buyer—only to discover that the actual final offer is lower.

Instead of asking only:

“What is the highest price you pay per gram?”

Also ask:

“How will you determine my final offer?”

A transparent evaluation should make it reasonably clear how the item’s weight, purity, current gold price, stones, and other characteristics affect the final amount.

Compare the money you can actually receive—not simply the biggest number mentioned before the jewelry has been evaluated.

Should Diamonds and Gemstones Be Valued Separately?

Yes, when they have meaningful resale value.

If a 14K gold ring contains a valuable diamond, calculating only the gold melt value may significantly underestimate the value of the entire piece.

The same can apply to certain:

  • Natural diamonds
  • GIA-graded diamonds
  • Sapphires
  • Rubies
  • Emeralds
  • Signed designer pieces
  • Vintage or estate jewelry

A knowledgeable jewelry buyer should determine whether the stones or the complete piece have value beyond the gold itself.

What About Designer 14K Gold Jewelry?

Designer jewelry should not automatically be treated as scrap.

Certain pieces from recognized luxury or designer brands can command secondary-market value beyond their raw gold content.

Before selling designer 14K jewelry, consider whether the piece has:

  • A recognizable maker’s mark
  • Original packaging
  • Documentation
  • Serial numbers
  • Distinctive design
  • Strong resale demand

If those factors are present, ask whether the buyer is evaluating the item as jewelry or simply calculating its scrap-gold value.

Pawn Shop vs. Gold Buyer for 14K Gold

Pawn shops and specialized gold buyers operate differently.

A pawn shop may purchase gold outright or offer a loan secured by the jewelry.

A dedicated gold and jewelry buyer typically focuses on purchasing precious metals, diamonds, watches, and jewelry directly.

Neither business type automatically guarantees a better price.

What matters is how accurately your property is evaluated and what final amount you are offered.

When comparing buyers, look for:

  • Transparent weighing
  • Proper purity testing
  • Clear explanation of the offer
  • Knowledge of diamonds and designer jewelry
  • Current market awareness
  • Strong local reputation
  • No-pressure evaluation

How to Compare 14K Gold Offers in Los Angeles

Los Angeles has a large jewelry and precious-metals market, particularly around the Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District.

That gives sellers choices, but it also makes comparing offers important.

Before accepting an offer:

  1. Know approximately how many grams your jewelry weighs.
  2. Look for a 14K, 14KT, 583, or 585 hallmark.
  3. Check the current gold market price.
  4. Estimate the theoretical gold content.
  5. Identify valuable diamonds, gemstones, or designer brands.
  6. Ask the buyer to explain how the offer was calculated.
  7. Compare actual final offers rather than preliminary quotes.

A few minutes of preparation can give you a much better understanding of what you’re being offered.

If you’re ready to compare local options, our guide to selling gold jewelry in Downtown Los Angeles explains what sellers should look for before choosing a buyer.

Can I Calculate My 14K Gold Value at Home?

You can create a useful estimate at home if you know the weight and approximate purity.

For a piece believed to be 14K:

Weight in grams × 0.583 × pure gold price per gram = estimated underlying gold value

For example, if you have 40 grams of 14K jewelry:

40 × 0.583 = approximately 23.32 grams of pure gold

You would then multiply 23.32 by the current pure gold price per gram.

This gives you a useful reference point before speaking with a buyer.

However, home calculations cannot determine every factor that might affect an actual offer, particularly when the jewelry contains stones or may have resale value as a complete piece.

Where Can I Sell 14K Gold in Los Angeles?

If you’re looking to sell 14K gold in Los Angeles, you have several options, including pawn shops, jewelry stores, precious-metal dealers, and dedicated gold buyers.

The best choice depends on what you’re selling.

Simple broken 14K jewelry may primarily be evaluated for gold content. A diamond engagement ring, designer bracelet, estate piece, luxury watch, or collectible item may require a more comprehensive evaluation.

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds in Downtown Los Angeles evaluates gold jewelry, diamonds, coins, watches, estate jewelry, and other valuable pieces.

An in-person evaluation allows the item’s weight, purity, stones, brand, condition, and potential resale value to be considered before an offer is made.

How to Prepare Your 14K Gold Before Selling

You generally do not need to professionally clean or repair gold jewelry before having it evaluated.

Instead:

  • Gather pieces you believe are gold.
  • Keep matching sets together.
  • Bring certificates or paperwork for important diamonds.
  • Bring boxes and documentation for designer pieces when available.
  • Avoid removing stones yourself.
  • Make a note of any known history or provenance for estate jewelry.

Most importantly, don’t assume that broken or old jewelry has little value. Gold retains intrinsic value even when the jewelry is damaged or no longer wearable.

Frequently Asked Questions About 14K Gold Value

How pure is 14K gold?

14K gold is approximately 58.3% pure gold. The remaining portion consists of other metals used to create the alloy.

What does 585 mean on gold jewelry?

A 585 marking generally indicates approximately 58.5% gold content and is commonly associated with 14K gold jewelry.

How do I calculate the 14K gold price per gram?

Determine the pure gold price per gram and multiply it by approximately 0.583. This provides an estimate of the underlying 14K gold melt value per gram.

Is the 14K gold price per gram the amount a buyer will pay me?

Not necessarily. The calculated melt value is a reference point. Actual offers can account for refining, processing, market risk, business costs, resale potential, stones, brand, and other characteristics.

Is 14K gold worth more than 10K gold?

Per gram, 14K gold generally has a higher underlying gold value than 10K gold because 14K contains a greater percentage of pure gold.

Is 18K gold worth more than 14K gold?

When comparing equal weights based strictly on gold content, 18K gold generally has a higher melt value because it contains 75% gold, compared with approximately 58.3% for 14K.

Are 14K white gold and 14K yellow gold worth the same?

When evaluated strictly for gold content, equal weights of genuine 14K white and yellow gold contain approximately the same proportion of pure gold. Other characteristics of the jewelry can still affect its total value.

Should I remove diamonds before selling my 14K gold ring?

Usually not. Have the complete ring professionally evaluated first. The diamond or other gemstones may have separate value.

Where can I get my 14K gold evaluated in Los Angeles?

Gold can be evaluated by professional precious-metal and jewelry buyers. In Downtown Los Angeles, sellers can compare buyers in and around the Jewelry District and ask for an explanation of how each final offer is calculated.

Final Thoughts: Know What Your 14K Gold Is Worth Before You Sell

Understanding the 14K gold price per gram gives you a valuable starting point before selling jewelry.

Remember the basic calculation:

Current pure gold price per gram × approximately 58.3% = estimated 14K gold melt value per gram

But don’t stop at the calculation.

Your jewelry may contain diamonds, gemstones, designer value, collectible value, or other characteristics that deserve consideration beyond its gold weight.

And when comparing gold buyers, focus on the final amount you can actually receive—not simply the highest preliminary quote.

If you’re considering selling, you can learn more about working with a Downtown Los Angeles gold buyer and what to expect during an in-person evaluation.

An informed seller is in a much stronger position to understand an evaluation, compare offers, and decide when the price is right.

A professional evaluation may also consider: Exact weight Verified gold purity Diamonds or gemstones Designer or luxury brand Condition Craftsmanship Collectibility Potential resale value Current market demand This is why simply searching “14K gold price today” cannot always tell you exactly what a particular piece of jewelry is worth. Does 14K Yellow, White, or Rose Gold Have the Same Gold Value? If each item is genuinely the same karat purity and weight, 14K yellow gold, 14K white gold, and 14K rose gold contain approximately the same proportion of pure gold. The different colors primarily come from the metals alloyed with the gold. Therefore, when jewelry is valued primarily for its gold content, color by itself usually does not create a major difference in the underlying gold value. However, a particular piece may still be worth more because of its brand, design, gemstones, condition, age, or resale demand. Why the Weight of Your 14K Gold Matters Gold buyers commonly evaluate precious metals using grams, pennyweights, or troy ounces. One troy ounce equals approximately 31.1035 grams. If you are comparing offers, make sure you understand which unit of measurement each buyer is using. A price quoted “per gram” cannot be directly compared with a price quoted “per pennyweight” without converting the units. You should also ask whether stones or other non-gold components are included in the displayed weight and how those components affect the calculation. Why a 14K Stamp Is Not the Entire Evaluation A 14K or 585 stamp is useful evidence, but a professional gold buyer may still test the jewelry. Stamps can wear down, jewelry can be repaired with different metals, and some pieces may contain multiple components with different purity levels. Depending on the item, a professional evaluation may include: Visual inspection Hallmark examination Accurate weighing Acid testing Electronic testing XRF analysis when appropriate Testing helps determine what is actually being purchased rather than relying only on a stamp. Melt Value vs. What a Gold Buyer Pays One of the most important concepts for gold sellers is the difference between melt value and a buyer’s actual offer. Melt value represents the theoretical value of the pure gold contained in the item based on the current market price. A buyer’s offer may be lower because a gold-buying business has costs associated with testing, processing, refining, market risk, overhead, and profit. On the other hand, some jewelry can be worth more than its basic melt value. A desirable designer bracelet, luxury-brand piece, antique item, collectible jewelry, or jewelry containing valuable diamonds may deserve an evaluation beyond its gold content alone. That is why automatically selling every piece strictly as scrap gold can sometimes leave money on the table. Our guide to how much you should get for gold jewelry explains the difference between underlying gold value and an actual purchase offer in greater detail. Highest Quote vs. Final Offer: Know the Difference When comparing gold buyers, don’t evaluate a buyer only by the highest price quoted over the phone or advertised online. The highest initial quote is not necessarily the highest amount you will actually receive. Some buyers may provide an unusually attractive preliminary estimate based on assumptions about weight, purity, condition, or market value. After the item is examined in person, the final offer may be substantially different. A very high initial number can also anchor a seller’s expectations. If competing buyers cannot match that quoted figure, the seller may return to the original buyer—only to discover that the actual final offer is lower. Instead of asking only: “What is the highest price you pay per gram?” Also ask: “How will you determine my final offer?” A transparent evaluation should make it reasonably clear how the item’s weight, purity, current gold price, stones, and other characteristics affect the final amount. Compare the money you can actually receive—not simply the biggest number mentioned before the jewelry has been evaluated. Should Diamonds and Gemstones Be Valued Separately? Yes, when they have meaningful resale value. If a 14K gold ring contains a valuable diamond, calculating only the gold melt value may significantly underestimate the value of the entire piece. The same can apply to certain: Natural diamonds GIA-graded diamonds Sapphires Rubies Emeralds Signed designer pieces Vintage or estate jewelry A knowledgeable jewelry buyer should determine whether the stones or the complete piece have value beyond the gold itself. What About Designer 14K Gold Jewelry? Designer jewelry should not automatically be treated as scrap. Certain pieces from recognized luxury or designer brands can command secondary-market value beyond their raw gold content. Before selling designer 14K jewelry, consider whether the piece has: A recognizable maker’s mark Original packaging Documentation Serial numbers Distinctive design Strong resale demand If those factors are present, ask whether the buyer is evaluating the item as jewelry or simply calculating its scrap-gold value. Pawn Shop vs. Gold Buyer for 14K Gold Pawn shops and specialized gold buyers operate differently. A pawn shop may purchase gold outright or offer a loan secured by the jewelry. A dedicated gold and jewelry buyer typically focuses on purchasing precious metals, diamonds, watches, and jewelry directly. Neither business type automatically guarantees a better price. What matters is how accurately your property is evaluated and what final amount you are offered. When comparing buyers, look for: Transparent weighing Proper purity testing Clear explanation of the offer Knowledge of diamonds and designer jewelry Current market awareness Strong local reputation No-pressure evaluation How to Compare 14K Gold Offers in Los Angeles Los Angeles has a large jewelry and precious-metals market, particularly around the Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District. That gives sellers choices, but it also makes comparing offers important. Before accepting an offer: Know approximately how many grams your jewelry weighs. Look for a 14K, 14KT, 583, or 585 hallmark. Check the current gold market price. Estimate the theoretical gold content. Identify valuable diamonds, gemstones, or designer brands. Ask the buyer to explain how the offer was calculated. Compare actual final offers rather than preliminary quotes. A few minutes of preparation can give you a much better understanding of what you’re being offered. If you’re ready to compare local options, our guide to selling gold jewelry in Downtown Los Angeles explains what sellers should look for before choosing a buyer. Can I Calculate My 14K Gold Value at Home? You can create a useful estimate at home if you know the weight and approximate purity. For a piece believed to be 14K: Weight in grams × 0.583 × pure gold price per gram = estimated underlying gold value For example, if you have 40 grams of 14K jewelry: 40 × 0.583 = approximately 23.32 grams of pure gold You would then multiply 23.32 by the current pure gold price per gram. This gives you a useful reference point before speaking with a buyer. However, home calculations cannot determine every factor that might affect an actual offer, particularly when the jewelry contains stones or may have resale value as a complete piece. Where Can I Sell 14K Gold in Los Angeles? If you’re looking to sell 14K gold in Los Angeles, you have several options, including pawn shops, jewelry stores, precious-metal dealers, and dedicated gold buyers. The best choice depends on what you’re selling. Simple broken 14K jewelry may primarily be evaluated for gold content. A diamond engagement ring, designer bracelet, estate piece, luxury watch, or collectible item may require a more comprehensive evaluation. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds in Downtown Los Angeles evaluates gold jewelry, diamonds, coins, watches, estate jewelry, and other valuable pieces. An in-person evaluation allows the item’s weight, purity, stones, brand, condition, and potential resale value to be considered before an offer is made. How to Prepare Your 14K Gold Before Selling You generally do not need to professionally clean or repair gold jewelry before having it evaluated. Instead: Gather pieces you believe are gold. Keep matching sets together. Bring certificates or paperwork for important diamonds. Bring boxes and documentation for designer pieces when available. Avoid removing stones yourself. Make a note of any known history or provenance for estate jewelry. Most importantly, don’t assume that broken or old jewelry has little value. Gold retains intrinsic value even when the jewelry is damaged or no longer wearable. Frequently Asked Questions About 14K Gold Value How pure is 14K gold? 14K gold is approximately 58.3% pure gold. The remaining portion consists of other metals used to create the alloy. What does 585 mean on gold jewelry? A 585 marking generally indicates approximately 58.5% gold content and is commonly associated with 14K gold jewelry. How do I calculate the 14K gold price per gram? Determine the pure gold price per gram and multiply it by approximately 0.583. This provides an estimate of the underlying 14K gold melt value per gram. Is the 14K gold price per gram the amount a buyer will pay me? Not necessarily. The calculated melt value is a reference point. Actual offers can account for refining, processing, market risk, business costs, resale potential, stones, brand, and other characteristics. Is 14K gold worth more than 10K gold? Per gram, 14K gold generally has a higher underlying gold value than 10K gold because 14K contains a greater percentage of pure gold. Is 18K gold worth more than 14K gold? When comparing equal weights based strictly on gold content, 18K gold generally has a higher melt value because it contains 75% gold, compared with approximately 58.3% for 14K. Are 14K white gold and 14K yellow gold worth the same? When evaluated strictly for gold content, equal weights of genuine 14K white and yellow gold contain approximately the same proportion of pure gold. Other characteristics of the jewelry can still affect its total value. Should I remove diamonds before selling my 14K gold ring? Usually not. Have the complete ring professionally evaluated first. The diamond or other gemstones may have separate value. Where can I get my 14K gold evaluated in Los Angeles? Gold can be evaluated by professional precious-metal and jewelry buyers. In Downtown Los Angeles, sellers can compare buyers in and around the Jewelry District and ask for an explanation of how each final offer is calculated. Final Thoughts: Know What Your 14K Gold Is Worth Before You Sell Understanding the 14K gold price per gram gives you a valuable starting point before selling jewelry. Remember the basic calculation: Current pure gold price per gram × approximately 58.3% = estimated 14K gold melt value per gram But don’t stop at the calculation. Your jewelry may contain diamonds, gemstones, designer value, collectible value, or other characteristics that deserve consideration beyond its gold weight. mainHtml:
Here’s the real talk: white gold and yellow gold are actually the same purity-wise, but they’re totally different when it comes to cost, upkeep, and how they look on your skin. If you’re trying to decide which one to buy, sell, or keep, you need to understand what you’re actually getting into.

What’s the Actual Difference Between White Gold and Yellow Gold?

Both white and yellow gold contain the exact same amount of pure gold. A 14K white gold ring has 14 parts gold out of 24, just like a 14K yellow gold ring. The karat number means the same thing for both colors.

So where’s the difference? The other metals mixed in. Yellow gold is the natural color of pure gold. White gold gets its color from alloys like palladium, nickel, or platinum that get blended into the gold. Then it gets coated with rhodium (a super shiny metal) to make it bright white and protect it from wear.

Cost: Which One Costs More?

White gold is almost always more expensive than yellow gold. Why? Because those added precious metals (palladium and platinum) cost real money, and the rhodium plating adds labor costs too.

Related: Platinum vs White Gold: Which Metal Is Right for You?

Related: White Gold: What It Is & Why It’s Worth So Much

The price gap isn’t huge, but it’s real. If you’re shopping for an engagement ring or a chain, expect to pay 10-15% more for white gold than you would for the same piece in yellow gold. Over time, that rhodium plating wears off and needs replating, which costs $50-$150 depending on the piece. Yellow gold? Just clean it and you’re done.

Maintenance: Yellow Gold Wins (Hands Down)

Yellow gold is nearly maintenance-free. You can wear it every single day for decades and it’ll look basically the same. A little cleaning with warm soapy water and you’re good.

White gold needs way more attention. That rhodium plating dulls over time, and once it does, you’ll notice the slightly yellowish color underneath showing through. Most people get their white gold replated every 3-5 years to keep it looking brand new. That’s an extra cost and hassle yellow gold doesn’t have.

Which One Looks Better on Your Skin?

This is personal, but there are some real rules. Yellow gold tends to look amazing on warm skin tones and medium-to-darker skin. It creates this natural glow and makes your skin look warmer.

White gold looks sharper and more modern on cool undertones and lighter skin. It creates contrast and gives off that clean, contemporary vibe.

But honestly? If you love a color, wear it. Don’t let skin tone rules stop you. The best metal is the one that makes you feel confident. That said, if you’re planning to sell your jewelry down the road, knowing what’s currently trending matters. Right now in 2026, Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds is seeing major demand for yellow gold pieces. Yellow gold is having a serious comeback after white gold dominated the market for the last decade. About 40% of all new engagement rings purchased are now in yellow gold.

Explore Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds →

Related: Best Yellow Gold Rings 2026: Top 5 Ranked & Compared

Related: Best 14K White Gold Rings 2026: Top 5 Ranked & Compared

Related: Best 10K White Gold Rings 2026: Top Options Ranked

Resale Value: What Actually Matters

Both white and yellow gold hold their value reasonably well, but the resale game is different for each. White gold loses some value because of that rhodium plating situation. Buyers know they’ll need to plate it again, so they factor that cost in. Yellow gold has no hidden costs, which makes it slightly easier to sell.

Related: Legitimate Gold Buyer vs Pawn Shop: Which Offers Better Prices?

The real value driver isn’t the color though. It’s the quality of the diamonds (if any), the weight of the gold, and the current market price per gram. A white gold ring with a low-quality diamond will sell for way less than a yellow gold ring with a great diamond, regardless of the metal color.

When you’re ready to sell, getting an expert evaluation makes all the difference. knowing what your 14K gold necklace is actually worth is the first step to getting fair market value.

Durability and Allergies

Both metals are durable enough for everyday wear. Yellow gold is slightly more durable because it’s pure gold with fewer alloys, but the difference is minimal for jewelry. White gold’s extra metals actually make it slightly harder, which is good for holding stones.

If you have nickel allergies or sensitive skin, higher karat gold is your friend. 18K yellow gold is safer than 14K because it has less nickel (and fewer alloys overall). 18K white gold is better than 14K white gold for the same reason. The higher the karat, the less nickel in the mix.

2026 Market Trends: Yellow Gold Is Back

Here’s something cool: yellow gold has reclaimed the top spot after a decade of white and platinum dominance. In 2015-2020, white gold was everywhere. Now? Yellow gold is having a major comeback, especially in engagement rings and statement pieces.

Fashion cycles are real. Younger buyers are favoring the warmth and nostalgia of yellow gold. If you’re sitting on a collection of older yellow gold pieces, now is actually a solid time to consider selling. The market is strong, and collectors are hunting for quality pieces.

Which Should You Choose?

If you want low maintenance and natural beauty, yellow gold is the move. If you want that bright, modern sparkle and don’t mind replating every few years, white gold works. If you’re buying an investment piece and plan to hold it long-term, yellow gold edges ahead because of resale simplicity.

Still unsure? Check out what actual customers say about selling gold to understand what real people prioritize when they’re making these decisions.

Ready to Sell Your Gold?

Whether you’ve got white gold, yellow gold, or a mix of both, understanding what you have is the first step to getting paid fairly. Learn how to get the best price for your gold with transparent evaluations and same-day cash payment. No pressure, no haggling, just honest assessments and fair offers.

If any of this resonated, give Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds a look — it is where the rest of our research lives.

Which gold color is worth more?

Both white and yellow gold have the same intrinsic value based on purity and weight. The price difference comes from manufacturing costs (white gold uses pricier alloys) and maintenance. Yellow gold is slightly easier to resell because there’s no replating cost down the line, but the difference in resale value is usually under 5%.

Why does white gold need replating?

Rhodium plating is a protective layer that gives white gold its bright, shiny appearance. Daily wear (especially on rings) causes this layer to thin over time. Eventually, the slightly yellow undertone of the actual gold shows through. Replating restores the white look and protects the metal underneath. Yellow gold doesn’t need this because its natural color doesn’t require a coating.

Does white gold or yellow gold scratch easier?

Yellow gold scratches more visibly because scratches show up on the yellow color. White gold shows scratches less obviously at first, but once that rhodium plating wears away, scratches and discoloration become noticeable. Neither is significantly more durable than the other in real-world use.

Can you wear white gold and yellow gold together?

Absolutely. Mixing metals is totally trendy right now. That said, white gold has a bright, cool tone and yellow gold has a warm tone. The contrast can look intentional and modern, or it can look chaotic if the pieces don’t coordinate well. If you’re planning to mix them, aim for a balanced look (like equal amounts of each) rather than random combinations.

If you’re buying an investment piece and plan to hold it long-term, yellow gold edges ahead because of resale simplicity. Still unsure? Check out what actual customers say about selling gold to understand what real people prioritize when they’re making these decisions. Ready to Sell Your Gold? Whether you’ve got white gold, yellow gold, or a mix of both, understanding what you have is the first step to getting paid fairly. Learn how to get the best price for your gold with transparent evaluations and same-day cash payment. No pressure, no haggling, just honest assessments and fair offers. If any of this resonated, give Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds a look — it is where the rest of our research lives. Which gold color is worth more? Both white and yellow gold have the same intrinsic value based on purity and weight. The price difference comes from manufacturing costs (white gold uses pricier alloys) and maintenance. Yellow gold is slightly easier to resell because there’s no replating cost down the line, but the difference in resale value is usually under 5%. Why does white gold need replating? Rhodium plating is a protective layer that gives white gold its bright, shiny appearance. Daily wear (especially on rings) causes this layer to thin over time. Eventually, the slightly yellow undertone of the actual gold shows through. Replating restores the white look and protects the metal underneath. Yellow gold doesn’t need this because its natural color doesn’t require a coating. Does white gold or yellow gold scratch easier? Yellow gold scratches more visibly because scratches show up on the yellow color. White gold shows scratches less obviously at first, but once that rhodium plating wears away, scratches and discoloration become noticeable. Neither is significantly more durable than the other in real-world use. Can you wear white gold and yellow gold together? Absolutely. Mixing metals is totally trendy right now. That said, white gold has a bright, cool tone and yellow gold has a warm tone. The contrast can look intentional and modern, or it can look chaotic if the pieces don’t coordinate well. If you’re planning to mix them, aim for a balanced look (like equal amounts of each) rather than random combinations.
