Diamond Buyers Los Angeles – Sell Your Diamonds for Cash

Discover What Your Diamond Is Worth Today

Book an Appointment

Looking for trusted diamond buyers in Los Angeles? Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds buys loose diamonds, GIA-graded diamonds, engagement rings, diamond jewelry, estate diamonds, and diamonds of many shapes, sizes, colors, and clarity grades.

Visit our Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District location for an in-person diamond evaluation. We examine the characteristics that affect a diamond’s resale value, including carat weight, cut, color, clarity, shape, condition, certification, and current market demand.

If your diamond has a GIA grading report or other documentation, bring it with you. Documentation can help us verify important characteristics of the stone, but we can also evaluate diamonds that do not have their original paperwork.

After evaluating your diamond, we can provide an offer based on the specific stone and current resale market conditions. There is no obligation to sell simply because you receive an evaluation.

Book a Diamond Evaluation

What Types of Diamonds Do We Buy in Los Angeles?

We evaluate many types of diamonds and diamond jewelry, including:

  • GIA-graded diamonds
  • Loose diamonds
  • Natural diamonds
  • Engagement rings
  • Diamond wedding rings
  • Diamond earrings
  • Diamond necklaces
  • Diamond bracelets
  • Estate and inherited diamond jewelry
  • Vintage diamond jewelry
  • Designer diamond jewelry
  • Diamonds set in gold or platinum jewelry

If you are unsure what you have, bring the item in for evaluation rather than trying to determine its value from photographs or online calculators alone.

Schedule Your Diamond Evaluation

Book a private appointment online, call us, or visit our Downtown Los Angeles location for an in-person diamond evaluation.

Expert Diamond Evaluation

We examine your diamond’s carat weight, cut, color, clarity, shape, condition, certification, and other factors that can affect its resale value.

Receive Your Offer

After the evaluation, we explain our offer so you can decide whether selling your diamond is right for you. If you accept the offer, available payment options may include cash, check, or bank transfer.

Speak With Us

Understanding Your Diamond Before You Sell

Selling a GIA Diamond in Los Angeles

A GIA grading report can provide important information about a diamond, including its carat weight, color, clarity, cut grade when applicable, measurements, proportions, and identifying characteristics.

If your diamond has its original GIA report, bring the report with you. We can use the grading information together with an inspection of the actual diamond and current market conditions when evaluating the stone.

A grading report does not by itself determine the amount a buyer will pay. Two diamonds with similar laboratory grades can have different resale demand and market values depending on characteristics such as shape, measurements, cut quality, fluorescence, condition, and current buyer demand.

How Is a Diamond’s Value Determined?

There is no single price-per-carat number that accurately values every diamond. Several characteristics work together to influence resale value.

Carat Weight

A diamond’s carat weight measures its weight, but larger diamonds do not simply increase in value at the same rate per carat. Size thresholds, quality, shape, and market demand can significantly affect value.

Cut

Cut and proportions affect how effectively a diamond reflects light and can influence both appearance and market desirability.

Color

For many colorless diamonds, less visible body color can affect grading and market value. Fancy-color diamonds are evaluated differently.

Clarity

Clarity considers inclusions and blemishes, including their size, number, position, and visibility.

Other important factors can include diamond shape, measurements, fluorescence, laboratory report, condition, brand or setting, and current wholesale and resale demand.

Sell Your Diamond Engagement Ring in Los Angeles

If you are selling a diamond engagement ring, we evaluate both the center diamond and the ring itself. Depending on the piece, factors such as additional diamonds, precious-metal content, designer branding, condition, and documentation may also affect the overall evaluation.

Bring any GIA reports, receipts, original boxes, designer documentation, or other paperwork you still have. These items are helpful when available, but they are not required for us to examine your jewelry.

Speak With Us

Why Sell Your Diamond to Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds?

Our goal is to make selling a diamond in Los Angeles straightforward and transparent. You can bring your diamond to our Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District location for an in-person evaluation and receive an offer based on the characteristics of your specific item and current market conditions.

There is no obligation to sell after receiving an evaluation.

  • In-person diamond evaluation
  • Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District location
  • GIA-graded and non-certified diamonds evaluated
  • Loose diamonds and diamond jewelry accepted
  • Engagement rings and estate jewelry evaluated
  • Clear explanation of the offer
  • No obligation to sell

Read our customer reviews to learn about other sellers’ experiences.

Get an Item-Specific Diamond Offer

When comparing diamond buyers, focus on the final offer for your actual diamond rather than relying only on an estimated price given before the stone is inspected.

A diamond’s value cannot be determined accurately from carat weight alone. The complete characteristics of the diamond and current market demand matter.

Ask how the offer was determined and compare final, item-specific offers before deciding where to sell.

Local Diamond Buyer vs. Consignment or Auction

There are several ways to sell a diamond. The right choice depends on whether your priority is convenience, speed, or potentially waiting for a future buyer.

Direct Local Diamond Buyer

A direct buyer evaluates the diamond and can make an offer for the item. This allows the seller to decide whether to accept an offer without waiting for the jewelry to sell to another consumer.

Consignment

With consignment, the jewelry is generally listed for sale and the seller waits for another buyer to purchase it. Terms, fees, and timelines vary by company.

Auction

Auction may be appropriate for certain rare, important, or highly desirable pieces. Auction fees, timing, reserves, and results vary depending on the auction house and item.

Have other items to sell? We also evaluate gold jewelry and luxury watches.

Book a Diamond Evaluation

Frequently Asked Questions About Selling Diamonds in Los Angeles

Where can I sell a diamond in Los Angeles?

Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds evaluates diamonds at our location in the Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District. We evaluate loose diamonds, engagement rings, diamond jewelry, estate pieces, and GIA-graded diamonds.

Do I need a GIA certificate to sell my diamond?

No. A GIA report or other laboratory documentation is helpful when available, but you can still bring a diamond for evaluation without its original paperwork.

What determines how much my diamond is worth?

Diamond value can depend on carat weight, cut, color, clarity, shape, measurements, condition, laboratory grading, fluorescence, and current resale demand.

Do you buy loose diamonds?

Yes. We evaluate loose diamonds as well as diamonds mounted in engagement rings and other jewelry.

Can I sell an engagement ring?

Yes. We evaluate diamond engagement rings and consider the center stone as well as relevant characteristics of the setting, additional stones, precious metals, branding, condition, and documentation.

Should I bring my GIA report?

Yes, if you have it. Bring the original GIA report and any other relevant documentation, receipts, boxes, or designer paperwork that may help identify the item.

How do I compare offers from diamond buyers?

Compare the final offer for your actual diamond and ask how the buyer determined the offer. Estimates given before physical inspection may change after the diamond’s characteristics are verified.

Is a diamond evaluation the same as an insurance appraisal?

Not necessarily. An insurance or replacement-value appraisal serves a different purpose from an offer to purchase a diamond in the current resale market.

Bring your loose diamond, engagement ring, or diamond jewelry to Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds in the Downtown Los Angeles Jewelry District for an in-person evaluation.

If you have a GIA report, receipt, box, or other documentation, bring it with you. If you do not have paperwork, we can still examine your diamond.

If you have a 10K gold ring, chain, bracelet, necklace, or broken jewelry sitting at home, one of the first questions you may ask is: How much is 10K gold worth per gram at a pawn shop?

There isn’t one fixed answer.

The 10K gold price per gram is subject to market fluctuations, so it’s essential to stay updated.

When estimating the 10K gold price per gram, remember that the purity affects the overall worth.

The 10K gold price per gram changes with the current gold market, and the amount a pawn shop or gold buyer offers can also depend on the weight of your jewelry, its actual purity, whether it contains stones or non-gold components, and whether the piece has additional resale value.

The 10K gold price per gram can vary based on the buyer’s evaluation standards.

The most important thing to understand before selling is that 10K gold is approximately 41.7% pure gold. That means the value of 10K jewelry can be estimated from the current price of pure gold, but the calculated gold value and the cash offer you receive are not necessarily the same amount.

If you’re considering selling your jewelry in Los Angeles, understanding this calculation can help you compare offers and make a more informed decision.

How Is the 10K Gold Price Per Gram Calculated?

The starting point for determining the value of 10K gold is the current spot price of gold.

Gold is normally quoted internationally by the troy ounce, and one troy ounce equals approximately 31.1035 grams.

Because 24K gold is considered essentially pure gold and 10K gold contains 10 parts gold out of 24, the theoretical purity of 10K gold is:

10 ÷ 24 = 41.67%

For accurate evaluations, reference the 10K gold price per gram.

So a simple estimate of the intrinsic gold value of 10K jewelry is:The 10K gold price per gram can serve as a reference point for negotiations.Understanding the 10K gold price per gram can maximize your selling potential.

Researching the 10K gold price per gram will empower your selling strategy.

Current pure gold price per gram × 41.67% = approximate 10K gold value per gram

For example, if pure gold were worth $100 per gram, the theoretical gold content of one gram of 10K gold would be worth approximately:

A buyer will consider the 10K gold price per gram when making an offer for your jewelry.

The 10K gold price per gram does not always reflect what pawn shops will pay.

$100 × 0.4167 = $41.67

Always check the latest 10K gold price per gram before visiting a buyer.

Often, the 10K gold price per gram will guide your expectations during transactions.

This is only an example—not today’s gold price or a guaranteed purchase price.

You can check the current market price through an established precious-metals market source such as GoldPrice.org before getting your jewelry evaluated.

How Much Do Pawn Shops Pay Per Gram for 10K Gold?

A pawn shop’s offer for 10K gold is generally not the same as the theoretical value of the pure gold contained in the jewelry.

A business purchasing gold needs to account for testing, processing, refining, market movement, overhead, and its own operating margin. Different businesses can therefore make different offers for the exact same piece.

This is why we do not recommend relying on a universal claim such as “pawn shops always pay 40% to 60% of gold value.”

There is no single percentage that applies to every pawn shop, every gold buyer, or every transaction.

Instead, when comparing offers, ask:

  • What karat did you test my jewelry at?
  • What is the total payable gold weight?
  • What gold market price are you using?
  • How was my offer calculated?
  • Are stones or other non-gold components being deducted from the weight?
  • Does the piece have resale, designer, collectible, or gemstone value beyond its melt value?

Knowing the answers gives you a much better basis for comparing buyers.

Why Is 10K Gold Worth Less Than 14K or 18K Gold?

The difference comes primarily from gold purity.

The most common gold purities used in jewelry include:

If two pieces have exactly the same weight, the higher-karat piece generally contains more pure gold and therefore has a higher intrinsic gold value.

For example, a 10-gram 10K chain contains approximately 4.17 grams of theoretical pure gold content, while a 10-gram 14K chain contains approximately 5.83 grams.

However, purity and weight aren’t always the entire story.

What Determines How Much Your 10K Gold Jewelry Is Worth?

When a professional buyer evaluates gold jewelry, several factors can affect its potential value.

1. Gold Purity

The first question is whether the piece is actually 10K.

Jewelry may be stamped 10K, 10KT, or 417, but markings alone should not always be relied upon. A buyer can test the item to verify its purity.

2. Weight

Gold jewelry is commonly weighed in grams.

The heavier the actual gold content of your piece, the greater its intrinsic metal value, assuming the same purity.

However, the gross weight of a piece isn’t necessarily all gold. Gemstones, watch movements, clasps, springs, steel components, and other materials may need to be considered separately.

3. Current Gold Spot Price

Gold prices fluctuate throughout the trading day.

That means an article giving you a fixed price such as “$20 per gram” can quickly become outdated.

A better approach is to understand the formula and check the current market before you sell.

4. Diamonds and Gemstones

If your 10K gold jewelry contains diamonds or other potentially valuable stones, the piece should not automatically be treated as nothing more than scrap gold.

The stones may have value separate from the gold.

This is especially important for diamond rings, estate jewelry, and higher-quality pieces.

5. Brand and Resale Value

Some jewelry can be worth more intact than its metal content alone.

Designer jewelry, collectible pieces, certain antique items, and desirable estate jewelry may deserve additional evaluation before being treated strictly as scrap.

That’s one reason choosing an experienced jewelry buyer can matter.

Here’s a simple hypothetical example.

Suppose you have a 10-gram 10K gold chain.

Because 10K gold is approximately 41.67% pure:

10 grams × 0.4167 = approximately 4.167 grams of pure gold content

Next, multiply that number by the current market price of pure gold per gram.

If pure gold were hypothetically trading at $100 per gram:

4.167 × $100 = $416.70

In this hypothetical example, approximately $416.70 represents the theoretical value of the contained gold before considering the buyer’s costs, margin, refining, deductions, or any additional resale value.

It does not mean a pawn shop or gold buyer will pay exactly $416.70.

That’s an important distinction when you’re researching how much 10K gold is worth.

Is 10K Gold Considered Scrap Gold?

It can be.

“Scrap gold” generally refers to gold being valued primarily for its precious-metal content rather than as a finished piece of jewelry.

Examples can include:

  • Broken gold chains
  • Bent rings
  • Single earrings
  • Damaged bracelets
  • Old or unwanted jewelry
  • Jewelry missing stones
  • Pieces that are difficult to resell intact

The good news is that broken gold can still have significant precious-metal value.

A broken 10K chain doesn’t suddenly stop containing gold because the clasp is damaged.

Pawn shops and dedicated gold buyers operate differently.

A pawn shop may provide both collateral loans and outright purchases. If you pawn an item, you’re borrowing money against it and can generally reclaim it by repaying the loan according to the agreement.

Selling is different: ownership transfers to the buyer.

A specialized gold and jewelry buyer generally focuses on evaluating and purchasing precious metals, jewelry, diamonds, coins, watches, and related valuables.

Neither business type should automatically be assumed to offer the highest price.

Instead, compare the actual offers.

There are several things you can do before accepting an offer.

Check the Gold Market

Know approximately where gold is trading before visiting a buyer.

You don’t need to become a commodities expert. You simply want a reference point for understanding your jewelry’s underlying gold content.

Look for markings such as 10K or 417.

Remember that gemstones and non-gold components can affect the payable gold weight.

Photographs can help identify an item, but an accurate purchase offer may require inspecting and testing the actual jewelry.

At an in-person evaluation, you can also ask questions about the weight, purity, stones, and how the offer was determined.

You don’t have to accept the first offer you receive.

A professional buyer can examine the jewelry, test its purity, weigh it, and evaluate other relevant characteristics.

However, sellers should be prepared to comply with any identification or transaction requirements that apply to the buyer and transaction.

If you have original paperwork for designer jewelry, diamonds, or other valuable pieces, bring it with you because documentation can sometimes help establish what you have.

Cleaning ordinary scrap gold generally does not increase the amount of pure gold contained in the piece.

A 10-gram 10K item doesn’t become more valuable as gold simply because it is shinier.

More importantly, aggressive polishing or improper chemical cleaning can potentially damage certain jewelry, gemstones, finishes, or collectible pieces.

If you’re unsure, leave the jewelry as it is and let the buyer evaluate it.

No marking should be treated as an absolute guarantee by itself.

Stamps can be misleading, altered, or counterfeit.

A professional evaluation may use appropriate testing methods to determine whether the piece is gold and estimate its purity.

mainHtml:
You have diamonds you want to sell, and you want answers today—not weeks of back-and-forth emails or lowball offers from online retailers you’ve never met. The good news: you don’t have to wait. A free diamond appraisal with same-day cash is real, it’s available right now in Los Angeles, and it’s a lot simpler than you might think.

If you’re holding inherited diamond rings, estate jewelry, or pieces you no longer wear, the path forward starts with a professional evaluation and a fair offer. That’s exactly what Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds specializes in. No pressure. No hidden fees. Just honest appraisals and immediate payment.

What a Free Diamond Appraisal Actually Means

Let’s be clear about terminology, because the word “free” gets thrown around loosely in the jewelry business.

Related: Loose Diamond Appraisal Downtown Los Angeles: Top 6 Ranked

A true free appraisal means you walk in, a certified gemologist evaluates your diamond—checking its carat weight, clarity, color, and cut—and you walk out with a written assessment and a cash offer, all at zero cost to you. You don’t pay to have the diamond looked at. You don’t pay to get the report. That’s the standard at reputable local buyers, and it’s the only way you should expect to be treated.

Some online retailers and chain jewelry stores charge appraisal fees or only offer free evaluations on diamonds purchased from them. That’s not what we’re talking about here. When you work with a local Downtown Los Angeles buyer like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, the appraisal is complimentary whether you decide to sell or not.

Related: Uncut Diamond Buyers in Downtown Los Angeles | Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds

Related: Best Sapphire & Diamond Jewelry Buyers in Los Angeles 2026

Related: Best Diamond Buyers Los Angeles 2026: Top 6 Ranked

Related: Best Certified Diamond Appraisers Los Angeles 2026: Top 5 Ranked

Why Same-Day Cash Matters When You Need Liquidity

Timing is everything. Maybe you’re settling an estate and need to liquidate inherited jewelry quickly. Maybe you’re going through a life change—a divorce, a move, a financial pivot—and you need immediate funds without the hassle of consignment or auction waiting periods.

Same-day cash means you don’t wait two weeks for payment to clear a bank account somewhere out of state. You don’t worry about shipping costs, insurance, or whether a buyer will actually honor their online quote. You get evaluated in person, you see the offer, and if you agree, the cash is yours before you leave.

Most reputable buyers in major markets now make same-day payment standard. A typical in-store appraisal takes 30 to 60 minutes depending on how many pieces you’re bringing and how complex the evaluation needs to be. Once you accept the offer, payment happens immediately.

How the Appraisal Process Works: Step by Step

You walk into a professional buyer’s location—no appointment necessary, though scheduling ahead can save you time. A certified gemologist sits with you, examines your diamond under magnification, and measures key properties.

They’re looking at:

  • Carat weight: The mass of the stone, measured to a specific decimal.
  • Clarity: The presence or absence of internal inclusions or surface blemishes.
  • Color: Graded on a scale from D (colorless) to Z (light color).
  • Cut: How well the diamond was shaped to reflect light and sparkle.

This is the “4Cs” framework used universally by GIA (Gemological Institute of America) certified appraisers. The appraiser compares your diamond against comparable sales data—real diamonds that sold recently at similar grades—and builds an offer based on current market value.

You get a written appraisal document you can take home. Many buyers now provide digital copies automatically. If you accept the offer, the transaction closes on the spot.

Local Buyer vs. Online Appraisal Tools: What’s the Real Difference

You’ve probably seen online diamond calculators that promise an appraisal in 60 seconds based on a photo. These tools exist, and they can give you a rough ballpark, but they’re not the same as a certified appraisal.

Online photo-based estimates use algorithms trained on comparable sales data, but they can’t account for the subtle things a gemologist sees in person: faint color shifts, tiny inclusions, polish quality, or symmetry issues that affect value. A photo simply doesn’t capture those details.

A professional in-person appraisal is the gold standard, especially if you’re making a selling decision. You get:

  • Direct conversation with someone who can explain the diamond’s grade and why it matters to price.
  • Transparency: you see the gemologist’s tools and methodology.
  • Certainty: an offer based on professional judgment, not algorithmic guessing.
  • Confidence: you know exactly what you’re selling and for how much before you commit.

This is why Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds and other trusted local buyers prioritize in-person evaluations. It’s faster, fairer, and it builds real trust.

Explore Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds →

Related: Diamond Price Guide 2026: What You’re Really Paying For

Related: Diamond Carat Weight: Complete Guide & Pricing

Related: Diamond Gems in Los Angeles: Your Complete Buying & Selling Guide

Related: Diamond Chart: The Complete 4Cs Guide for Buyers & Sellers

What Certifications and Credentials Actually Matter

Not every person calling themselves a gemologist has the same training. The credible standard is GIA certification—the Gemological Institute of America. A GIA-certified gemologist has completed rigorous coursework in diamond grading and has passed exams proving they can evaluate stones consistently and accurately.

When you’re getting an appraisal, ask if the evaluator is GIA-certified. It’s a simple question, and the answer tells you whether you’re working with someone trained to professional standards or someone who’s self-taught.

Some appraisers are also independent appraisers insured for appraisal work, which means they carry professional liability insurance. This is another mark of legitimacy, especially if you need the appraisal for insurance, estate, or legal purposes.

Red Flags: What Not to Accept

Before you hand over your diamonds, know what a legitimate buyer looks like:

  • They don’t pressure you to sell immediately.
  • They don’t charge you for the appraisal or evaluation.
  • They offer transparent pricing (they can explain exactly why your diamond is worth what they’re offering).
  • They’re happy to let you compare offers from other buyers if you want to.
  • They have a physical location you can visit and speak to a real person.

If a buyer is pushing hard, charging fees upfront, or refusing to explain their offer, walk out. The market is competitive, and you have options. A trustworthy buyer like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds is confident enough in their offer to let you make an informed decision.

Getting the Best Offer: What You Should Know Before Walking In

You don’t need to know your diamond’s grade before you arrive for an appraisal, but it helps to know what you have. If your diamond came with a GIA certificate, bring it. That certificate is the appraiser’s shortcut—they don’t have to re-grade the stone from scratch.

If you don’t have a certificate, that’s fine. The appraisal is still free, and the buyer will grade the diamond in front of you.

One more tip: diamond prices fluctuate based on market conditions. According to the Gemological Institute of America, factors like supply, lab-grown diamond availability, and jewelry demand all influence the wholesale value of diamonds. A buyer’s offer reflects the current market, not an arbitrary number.

If you’re selling multiple pieces—say, diamond rings and loose stones—bring them all. Buyers sometimes offer packages that are more favorable than individual evaluations.

Related: Loose Diamonds Appraised in Los Angeles – Expert Guide

Same-Day Cash: The Logistics That Actually Work

When you agree to sell, here’s what happens next. The buyer confirms the offer in writing, you sign paperwork confirming the sale, and the buyer hands you cash or, if you prefer, a cashier’s check or bank transfer (most buyers offer multiple payment methods for your security).

This all typically happens within an hour of your arrival. You don’t wait for the appraiser to consult with management or send the diamond somewhere else for verification. Local buyers keep things simple because they’ve been doing this for years and they trust their own staff.

At Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds, the standard since 2007 has been same-day payment. They’ve been in Downtown Los Angeles long enough to have built a reputation on speed and fairness.

When to Get Multiple Appraisals and When You Probably Don’t Need To

There’s no harm in getting a second opinion, especially if you’re selling a high-value diamond or if the first offer seems surprisingly high or surprisingly low. Most professional buyers don’t mind if you shop around.

That said, if you’re selling a standard diamond ring or estate piece and the appraisal makes sense to you—the appraiser explained the 4Cs clearly, the offer is fair relative to what you researched, and you trust the buyer—you don’t need to visit five different locations. You’re wasting time and creating decision fatigue.

A good rule of thumb: if the first appraisal is professional and transparent, and the buyer’s reputation is solid, you can feel confident moving forward.

How long does a diamond appraisal actually take?

A typical appraisal takes 30 to 60 minutes in-store, depending on the diamond’s complexity and the number of stones you’re having evaluated. Simpler stones with fewer inclusions grade faster. If you’re selling multiple pieces or vintage diamonds that need closer inspection, budget more time. Many buyers now offer appointment scheduling to ensure you’re not waiting around.

What do I need to bring for a free appraisal?

Just the diamond or diamond jewelry itself. If you have a GIA certificate or any paperwork that came with the stone, bring that too—it speeds up the process. You don’t need insurance documents, previous appraisals, or anything else unless you’re asking the buyer to verify specific information. Show up with the item and your ID, and you’re good to go.

What if I don’t like the offer? Can I walk away?

Absolutely. A free appraisal means exactly that—you’re under no obligation to sell. If the offer doesn’t match your expectations, say no thanks and leave with your diamond. Reputable buyers like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds build their business on trust, not pressure. You’re doing them a favor by considering their offer, and they understand that you might take it elsewhere.

Is same-day cash safe for high-value diamonds?

Yes, if you’re working with a legitimate buyer. Reputable companies carry commercial liability insurance and maintain secure locations. They handle high-value items routinely and follow strict protocols. That said, if you’re comfortable with a bank transfer or cashier’s check instead of cash, most buyers offer that option—it’s actually safer for you from a record-keeping perspective, because you have documentation of the transaction.

When to Get Multiple Appraisals and When You Probably Don’t Need To There’s no harm in getting a second opinion, especially if you’re selling a high-value diamond or if the first offer seems surprisingly high or surprisingly low. Most professional buyers don’t mind if you shop around. That said, if you’re selling a standard diamond ring or estate piece and the appraisal makes sense to you—the appraiser explained the 4Cs clearly, the offer is fair relative to what you researched, and you trust the buyer—you don’t need to visit five different locations. You’re wasting time and creating decision fatigue. A good rule of thumb: if the first appraisal is professional and transparent, and the buyer’s reputation is solid, you can feel confident moving forward. How long does a diamond appraisal actually take? A typical appraisal takes 30 to 60 minutes in-store, depending on the diamond’s complexity and the number of stones you’re having evaluated. Simpler stones with fewer inclusions grade faster. If you’re selling multiple pieces or vintage diamonds that need closer inspection, budget more time. Many buyers now offer appointment scheduling to ensure you’re not waiting around. What do I need to bring for a free appraisal? Just the diamond or diamond jewelry itself. If you have a GIA certificate or any paperwork that came with the stone, bring that too—it speeds up the process. You don’t need insurance documents, previous appraisals, or anything else unless you’re asking the buyer to verify specific information. Show up with the item and your ID, and you’re good to go. What if I don’t like the offer? Can I walk away? Absolutely. A free appraisal means exactly that—you’re under no obligation to sell. If the offer doesn’t match your expectations, say no thanks and leave with your diamond. Reputable buyers like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds build their business on trust, not pressure. You’re doing them a favor by considering their offer, and they understand that you might take it elsewhere. Is same-day cash safe for high-value diamonds? Yes, if you’re working with a legitimate buyer. Reputable companies carry commercial liability insurance and maintain secure locations. They handle high-value items routinely and follow strict protocols. That said, if you’re comfortable with a bank transfer or cashier’s check instead of cash, most buyers offer that option—it’s actually safer for you from a record-keeping perspective, because you have documentation of the transaction. mainHtml:
A Rolex Day Date in gold is one of the most recognizable luxury watches ever made. It’s the “President” watch—the one with two windows showing both the day of the week and the date. If you own one or are thinking about selling one, here’s what you actually need to know about pricing, value, and what makes these watches so sought-after.

What Is a Rolex Day Date Gold?

The Rolex Day Date is a dress watch designed specifically for gold or platinum. You won’t find a steel version—that’s what makes it exclusive. It debuted in 1956 and became the favorite of presidents, CEOs, and collectors who wanted something that said “I’ve arrived” without screaming about it.

Related: How to Sell a Rolex Watch in Los Angeles: Cash Today

The watch features the iconic President bracelet—solid gold links that flow like liquid when you wear them. It’s got a fluted bezel, a clean dial, and those two helpful windows at 12 and 3 o’clock. You get the full day spelled out and the date in a single glance.

Rolex makes the Day Date in two sizes: 36mm and 40mm. The 36mm is the classic, vintage-feeling option. The 40mm feels more modern and substantial on the wrist.

How Much Does a Rolex Day Date Gold Actually Cost?

Retail prices for a new Rolex Day Date gold start around $21,000 for an entry-level solid yellow gold model. A 40mm white gold version (reference 228239) sits at roughly $51,600. If you go for a diamond-set variant or a rare platinum piece, you’re looking at prices north of $100,000.

Related: White Gold: What It Is & Why It’s Worth So Much

That’s just the retail floor. On the secondary market, prices vary wildly depending on age, condition, and demand. A pre-owned model in good condition might sell for anywhere from $15,000 to $60,000, depending on the specific reference and year.

Gold prices themselves matter too. When gold is up, your watch value goes up. When gold dips, so does the resale value of your timepiece. If you’re thinking about selling, timing can affect what you get paid.

Why Do People Want Rolex Day Date Gold Watches?

Rolex Day Date gold watches hold value because of three things: the brand reputation, the precious metal content, and the timeless design.

First, Rolex is Rolex. It’s the most trusted name in watches. People know it, respect it, and want to own it. That trust translates directly into resale value.

Second, these watches are made from solid 18-karat gold or platinum. You’re not just buying a watch—you’re buying metal that has intrinsic value. Even if the watch stopped working tomorrow, the gold alone would be worth something.

Related: What Is 14 Karat Gold? Purity, Durability & Value

Third, the design never gets old. The Day Date looks nearly identical today as it did in 1956. That timelessness means it won’t look dated in your collection or in someone else’s.

How to Tell If Your Day Date Gold Is Real

If you own one, you probably know it’s real. But if you inherited one or are considering buying one, here are the key things to check.

  • Weight: A real gold Day Date feels substantial. Fake gold watches are often too light.
  • Bracelet links: Real President bracelets have solid gold links with clean welds. Fakes often have visible gaps or rough soldering.
  • Movement: Open the caseback and look at the movement. Rolex uses clean, precise finishing. Counterfeit movements look rough.
  • Serial number: Rolex stamps a unique serial number on the case. You can verify it with an authorized dealer.
  • Dial printing: The text on the dial should be crisp and evenly spaced. Fakes often have blurry or uneven printing.

If you’re unsure, get it authenticated by a professional. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds in Downtown Los Angeles can evaluate your watch for free and give you a clear answer about authenticity and current market value.

Explore Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds →

Should You Sell Your Rolex Day Date Gold?

That depends on your situation. If you need cash now, the secondary market is active. Gold watches sell. If you love it and can keep it, there’s something to be said for owning a piece of horological history that also holds value.

The market for pre-owned luxury watches is healthier than it’s been in years. Buyers actively seek out Day Date pieces, especially in good condition. You should get a fair offer relatively quickly.

One thing to consider: gold watches are less volatile than sports models like the Submariner or Daytona. You’re less likely to see wild price swings, but you’re also not going to see the crazy appreciation that a steel sports Rolex might experience.

Where to Sell Your Rolex Day Date Gold

You have a few options.

Online retailers and auction sites exist, but shipping a valuable watch across the country adds risk. Insurance, shipping delays, and disputes can turn a clean sale into a headache.

Local dealers and jewelers are solid if you know them. Get multiple appraisals, though. Prices can vary significantly depending on who’s evaluating it.

The best move is to work with a local buyer who specializes in luxury watches and has a solid reputation. Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds has been buying and evaluating luxury watches since 2007. You walk in, they assess your watch on the spot, they give you a transparent offer, and if you like it, you get paid the same day. No shipping. No waiting. No uncertainty.

You keep the power. If the offer isn’t what you hoped for, you walk out with your watch. No pressure, no hassle.

What Affects the Value of Your Day Date Gold?

Several things matter when someone evaluates your watch.

  • Condition: Is the dial pristine or does it have wear? Are the hands original? Does the bracelet have scratches or is it polished to perfection?
  • Service history: Has it been maintained by Rolex or an authorized service center? Original service records add value.
  • Completeness: Do you have the original box, papers, and warranty card? These increase value, though they’re not required.
  • Reference and year: Certain references and production years are more desirable. Vintage pieces from the 1960s and 1970s can command premiums.
  • Gold purity: 18k gold is standard for Rolex. Some vintage models used 14k. The purity affects both the metal value and collector value.

Gold Prices and Your Watch Value

Gold is a commodity. Its price fluctuates based on market demand, geopolitical events, and interest rates. When gold prices rise, your watch’s metal value rises with it. When gold drops, so does your watch’s baseline value.

For reference on current precious metal prices, you can check the NIST precious metals standards, though most buyers will use London Bullion Market pricing as their benchmark.

The reality: your Day Date gold watch is worth the gold inside it, plus whatever premium someone will pay for the Rolex name, condition, and collectibility. That total number changes slightly based on metal prices.

What To Expect When You Sell

If you decide to move forward, here’s the typical process with a reputable local buyer like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds: you bring the watch in, they examine it for authenticity and condition, they verify the reference and movement, they run the numbers based on current gold prices and market demand, they make you an offer, and if you accept, you get paid immediately in cash.

The whole thing usually takes 30-45 minutes. You leave with money in your pocket the same day. That beats waiting for an online auction to close or dealing with shipping logistics.

How much is my Rolex Day Date gold worth right now?

It depends on the reference, year, condition, and current gold prices. Entry-level solid gold models trade for $15,000 to $35,000 on the secondary market. White gold and platinum pieces run higher. The only way to know your specific watch’s value is to have it evaluated in person. Bring it to Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds in Downtown LA and get a free appraisal.

Are Rolex Day Date gold watches a good investment?

They’re a store of value rather than a get-rich-quick investment. You’re investing in a durable luxury item made of real gold that holds its baseline value even if the watch mechanism fails. Unlike a steel sports Rolex, a gold Day Date won’t appreciate wildly, but it also won’t tank. It’s a safe, conservative collectible.

Can I sell a Rolex Day Date gold without papers or original box?

Yes. The papers and box are nice to have and add value, but they’re not required to sell. A genuine Day Date gold with a good movement and clean condition will sell without them. You’ll likely get 5-10% less than one with complete documentation, but it’s still very sellable.

How do I know if my Day Date gold is worth selling now or waiting?

If you need the cash, sell now. Don’t time the market hoping gold prices go up. If you’re in no rush, watch gold prices over a few months and sell when they’re higher. But honestly, the difference is usually small. The bigger factor is the condition and reference of your specific watch. If you have a nice example in good shape, it will sell well regardless of tiny fluctuations in gold prices.

Gold purity: 18k gold is standard for Rolex. Some vintage models used 14k. The purity affects both the metal value and collector value. Gold Prices and Your Watch Value Gold is a commodity. Its price fluctuates based on market demand, geopolitical events, and interest rates. When gold prices rise, your watch’s metal value rises with it. When gold drops, so does your watch’s baseline value. For reference on current precious metal prices, you can check the NIST precious metals standards, though most buyers will use London Bullion Market pricing as their benchmark. The reality: your Day Date gold watch is worth the gold inside it, plus whatever premium someone will pay for the Rolex name, condition, and collectibility. That total number changes slightly based on metal prices. What To Expect When You Sell If you decide to move forward, here’s the typical process with a reputable local buyer like Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds: you bring the watch in, they examine it for authenticity and condition, they verify the reference and movement, they run the numbers based on current gold prices and market demand, they make you an offer, and if you accept, you get paid immediately in cash. The whole thing usually takes 30-45 minutes. You leave with money in your pocket the same day. That beats waiting for an online auction to close or dealing with shipping logistics. How much is my Rolex Day Date gold worth right now? It depends on the reference, year, condition, and current gold prices. Entry-level solid gold models trade for $15,000 to $35,000 on the secondary market. White gold and platinum pieces run higher. The only way to know your specific watch’s value is to have it evaluated in person. Bring it to Cash 4 Gold & Diamonds in Downtown LA and get a free appraisal. Are Rolex Day Date gold watches a good investment? They’re a store of value rather than a get-rich-quick investment. You’re investing in a durable luxury item made of real gold that holds its baseline value even if the watch mechanism fails. Unlike a steel sports Rolex, a gold Day Date won’t appreciate wildly, but it also won’t tank. It’s a safe, conservative collectible. Can I sell a Rolex Day Date gold without papers or original box? Yes. The papers and box are nice to have and add value, but they’re not required to sell. A genuine Day Date gold with a good movement and clean condition will sell without them. You’ll likely get 5-10% less than one with complete documentation, but it’s still very sellable. How do I know if my Day Date gold is worth selling now or waiting? If you need the cash, sell now. Don’t time the market hoping gold prices go up. If you’re in no rush, watch gold prices over a few months and sell when they’re higher. But honestly, the difference is usually small. The bigger factor is the condition and reference of your specific watch. If you have a nice example in good shape, it will sell well regardless of tiny fluctuations in gold prices. mainHtml:
Fake Watches hurt the authentic watch industry. Rolex is a luxury watch brand; everyone can’t afford these luxury watches because Rolex watches are expensive. These fake watches are often sold at suspiciously low prices, tempting unsuspecting buyers to purchase them. You can estimate the amount of fake rolex by this that many Rolexes are being sold even though brands haven’t produced them.

If you know how to spot a Fake Rolex, you can avoid wasting your money on a counterfeit or fake watch. In this article,

IS FAKE ROLEX A REAL PROBLEM?

Fake Rolex is a significant issue that customers are facing. Authentic Real watch brands like Rolex Submariner, Rolex Day-Date, and Rolex Datejust, have attracted counterfeiters. As I have discussed above they are produced in large quantities and often sold at suspiciously low prices, tempting those who may not be able to afford a genuine Rolex.

You will not lose your money and it always causes a decrease in the worth of Real Rolex brands because people reduce their trust in brands. Fake watches are made in different ways and may not last long but the effect they leave is that which can damage the brands’ reputations.

They are made with such precision that even an experienced person can be fooled to understand how much this  Rolex is fake or real. If you don’t know what you have to look for we will discuss it in the article so attached to us.

What types of Fake Rolex are Available in the Market

There are many ways to spot a fake Rolex but Fakes are usually categorized into three types we will discuss Here:

  •  Easy to spot: Bad fakes
  • All about the details: Good fakes and ‘supercolonies’
  • Putting parts together: Frankenstein watches

Now we will discuss these three one by one. so Let’s get started.

1. Easy to spot: Bad fakes:

As I have discussed above, fakes are usually categorized into three main types, but we will discuss first Bad fakes. You realize this when you visit the market, even if you are on holiday, and you see such types of Rolex. They are not real Rolex; they have just the name Rolex and the crown Rolex Watches logo.

You can see them alongside the bags and caps. These watches are completely fake and do not look like genuine Rolex. They should be furnished like a Rolex, but they can’t be because Rolex is not so cheap, which means you can’t watch them on the road. They are brands that are not available in such types of places or even in low-priced places.

Some watches that don’t exist in the official Rolex catalog are available in the market and are made by fake manufacturers. For example, they make Date without the day window, a Submariner with a GMT bezel, or even worse—a Daytona Chronograph with a rotating tachymeter bezel. You know, if tachymeter bezels can rotate, then they will not work properly.

Now tell me such type of fault will be made by Rolex no they do not make such type of fault.  In real Rolex watches you can’t see spelling errors on the dial or the word “quartz,” except in the ‘Oysterquartz’ models. Rolex only used quartz in those models, not in any others.

2. All about the details: Good fakes and ‘supercolonies:

Now we will discuss the second type of fake which is good Rolex and we can also say that they are called ‘super clones. These types of watches are produced in a way that you can’t distinguish between them.

One key giveaway is the lettering on the dial. Rolex watches have perfectly aligned text without fading. If you see a  with a slightly off font Rolex’s a strong spot that it might be a fake. The Cyclops lens on Rolex models magnifies the date 2.5x, which makes it difficult to replicate them it helps in spotting fake watches.

You can also spot fake watches by Rolex weight & material, and serial numbers on the Rehaut Rolex, Finally, verifying the movement should be done smoothly, as counterfeit movements often perform poorly compared to genuine ones. we will these each and everything here

3. Mixing of parts together: Frankenstein watches

The last and third are Frankenstein watches which are watches in which real Rolex components are mixed with fake components to make Frankenstein watches.

Watches with aftermarket dials or bracelets may look authentic but contain both genuine and counterfeit parts. Be cautious of pieces like a vintage Rolex Datejust with a non-original “Tiffany” dial, as they can compromise authenticity and value.

How to Spot a Fake Rolex: Important Fake Signs It’s Not the Real Thing

How do you identify a counterfeit when the Rolex watch model appears authentic? Knowing how to differentiate a genuine Rolex will make it simple to identify a fake.

Rolex Watch Weight:

You Always keep in mind its weight while buying a Rolex You can find its actual weight on Google by searching its model if it’s according to the Rolex model then buy it otherwise it’s fake go to the next store and follow the same step You have to keep in mind rolex heavier than a counterfeit watches. Always buy from an official Rolex dealer to guarantee that the products being sold are legitimate, even on pre-owned Rolex watches.

You can know a watch isn’t authentic if its cost sounds too good to be true. Vintage Rolexes are hollow weight due to their hollow bracelet links, but even then, they will be heftier than fake watches. If you feel it’s weight-light, it will likely be fake. After all, Rolex watches are extremely costly because they are designed using superior materials and expertise.

Serial Number: 

A Real Rolex has a serial number that is deeply engraved on the metal surface while in a fake it’s attached with an acid that may be removed after using some time. check the location of Rolex to authenticate whether it is real or fake. To check the serial number and look at where the bands connect to the lug. On the real Rolex serial number you can on the inner of the Rolex bezel

Model Number:

It is necessary to check the model number of watches to check Rolex’s authenticity.it is mentioned in the 12 0 clock side of the watch where the band and the lug meet. There should be an engraving “Rolex design”  on top of the model number. To verify that model number or design you have to use a paper clip to remove the pin that keeps the bands in place

Hand Motion:

Rolex watches have smooth and soundless second-hand motion, while fake watches have a ticking motion. While buying, look closely and listen carefully if it has a ticking sound, then it is a fake watch, not real. In Rolex watches, only the Oysterquartz is different; it uses a quartz movement, which causes it to tick like a quartz watch.

Cyclops Lens:

Real Rolex has a special lens called a “cyclops”.it’s shows the date as 2.5 times bigger. This lens on fake watches may have low quality and may not be aligned correctly or it may not magnify correctly. This feature of Cyclops is only available on real Rolex if you find another Rolex that has low quality lens that is not aligned correctly then it is fake maybe this type of watch falls in Frankenstein watches

Judge the Winding Crown :

There is a nob on the side of the watch. This is used to set time is called crown. A real Rolex has a logo on a crown it is made from a single piece of metal with fine details. On the other side, The fake Rolex crown logo is made from two or more pieces of metal that are joined together. To verify that the watch is genuine or fake use a magnifying glass to inspect the crown and logo closely.

Waterproof capability:

If Rolex has no waterproof then it’s fake. Each Rolex watch has a specific waterproof capability. Rolex Oyster Perpetual watches are guaranteed to be water-resistant up to 330 feet, whereas Rolex Submariner watches can withstand water depths of up to 1,000 feet.

A Rolex Sea Dweller can descend to depths of 4,000 feet, while the top model, the Rolex Sea Dweller Deepsea, can endure underwater pressures up to 12,800 feet. Now we can say that The Rolex watch is known for its waterproof capability.

Date Appears Bigger:

The Cyclops is a lens that is used in Real Rolex and shows the date as 2.5 times bigger. To check for Rolex authenticity, move your finger on the watch crystal; you should feel a bump on the convex lens covering the date. If you feel Cyclops is flat then it is fake.

Another method to test the authenticity is to hold the watch sideways and observe the date without Cyclops if the size of the date is unchanged then it is not a genuine Rolex watch.

How to stay safe:

To stay safe you have to follow the above important points while buying an authentic Rolex. Always try to buy from it trusted seller and read reviews and ask for references. Purchasing from a certified seller will increase your level of confidence in your new Watches.  Find your cherished watch, wear it with pride, and enjoy the search for your next treasure.

Another method to test the authenticity is to hold the watch sideways and observe the date without Cyclops if the size of the date is unchanged then it is not a genuine Rolex watch. Understanding the purity (karat) and weight of your gold items can help you estimate their value. Gold is typically measured in karats, with 24 karats being pure gold. The higher the karat, the more valuable the gold. Weighing your items can also give you an idea of their worth based on current market prices.

mainHtml:
Fake Watches hurt the authentic watch industry. Rolex is a luxury watch brand; everyone can’t afford these luxury watches because Rolex watches are expensive. These fake watches are often sold at suspiciously low prices, tempting unsuspecting buyers to purchase them. You can estimate the amount of fake rolex by this that many Rolexes are being sold even though brands haven’t produced them.

If you know how to spot a Fake Rolex, you can avoid wasting your money on a counterfeit or fake watch. In this article,

IS FAKE ROLEX A REAL PROBLEM?

Fake Rolex is a significant issue that customers are facing. Authentic Real watch brands like Rolex Submariner, Rolex Day-Date, and Rolex Datejust, have attracted counterfeiters. As I have discussed above they are produced in large quantities and often sold at suspiciously low prices, tempting those who may not be able to afford a genuine Rolex.

You will not lose your money and it always causes a decrease in the worth of Real Rolex brands because people reduce their trust in brands. Fake watches are made in different ways and may not last long but the effect they leave is that which can damage the brands’ reputations.

They are made with such precision that even an experienced person can be fooled to understand how much this  Rolex is fake or real. If you don’t know what you have to look for we will discuss it in the article so attached to us.

What types of Fake Rolex are Available in the Market

There are many ways to spot a fake Rolex but Fakes are usually categorized into three types we will discuss Here:

  •  Easy to spot: Bad fakes
  • All about the details: Good fakes and ‘supercolonies’
  • Putting parts together: Frankenstein watches

Now we will discuss these three one by one. so Let’s get started.

1. Easy to spot: Bad fakes:

As I have discussed above, fakes are usually categorized into three main types, but we will discuss first Bad fakes. You realize this when you visit the market, even if you are on holiday, and you see such types of Rolex. They are not real Rolex; they have just the name Rolex and the crown Rolex Watches logo.

You can see them alongside the bags and caps. These watches are completely fake and do not look like genuine Rolex. They should be furnished like a Rolex, but they can’t be because Rolex is not so cheap, which means you can’t watch them on the road. They are brands that are not available in such types of places or even in low-priced places.

Some watches that don’t exist in the official Rolex catalog are available in the market and are made by fake manufacturers. For example, they make Date without the day window, a Submariner with a GMT bezel, or even worse—a Daytona Chronograph with a rotating tachymeter bezel. You know, if tachymeter bezels can rotate, then they will not work properly.

Now tell me such type of fault will be made by Rolex no they do not make such type of fault.  In real Rolex watches you can’t see spelling errors on the dial or the word “quartz,” except in the ‘Oysterquartz’ models. Rolex only used quartz in those models, not in any others.

2. All about the details: Good fakes and ‘supercolonies:

Now we will discuss the second type of fake which is good Rolex and we can also say that they are called ‘super clones. These types of watches are produced in a way that you can’t distinguish between them.

One key giveaway is the lettering on the dial. Rolex watches have perfectly aligned text without fading. If you see a  with a slightly off font Rolex’s a strong spot that it might be a fake. The Cyclops lens on Rolex models magnifies the date 2.5x, which makes it difficult to replicate them it helps in spotting fake watches.

You can also spot fake watches by Rolex weight & material, and serial numbers on the Rehaut Rolex, Finally, verifying the movement should be done smoothly, as counterfeit movements often perform poorly compared to genuine ones. we will these each and everything here

3. Mixing of parts together: Frankenstein watches

The last and third are Frankenstein watches which are watches in which real Rolex components are mixed with fake components to make Frankenstein watches.

Watches with aftermarket dials or bracelets may look authentic but contain both genuine and counterfeit parts. Be cautious of pieces like a vintage Rolex Datejust with a non-original “Tiffany” dial, as they can compromise authenticity and value.

How to Spot a Fake Rolex: Important Fake Signs It’s Not the Real Thing

How do you identify a counterfeit when the Rolex watch model appears authentic? Knowing how to differentiate a genuine Rolex will make it simple to identify a fake.

Rolex Watch Weight:

You Always keep in mind its weight while buying a Rolex You can find its actual weight on Google by searching its model if it’s according to the Rolex model then buy it otherwise it’s fake go to the next store and follow the same step You have to keep in mind rolex heavier than a counterfeit watches. Always buy from an official Rolex dealer to guarantee that the products being sold are legitimate, even on pre-owned Rolex watches.

You can know a watch isn’t authentic if its cost sounds too good to be true. Vintage Rolexes are hollow weight due to their hollow bracelet links, but even then, they will be heftier than fake watches. If you feel it’s weight-light, it will likely be fake. After all, Rolex watches are extremely costly because they are designed using superior materials and expertise.

Serial Number: 

A Real Rolex has a serial number that is deeply engraved on the metal surface while in a fake it’s attached with an acid that may be removed after using some time. check the location of Rolex to authenticate whether it is real or fake. To check the serial number and look at where the bands connect to the lug. On the real Rolex serial number you can on the inner of the Rolex bezel

Model Number:

It is necessary to check the model number of watches to check Rolex’s authenticity.it is mentioned in the 12 0 clock side of the watch where the band and the lug meet. There should be an engraving “Rolex design”  on top of the model number. To verify that model number or design you have to use a paper clip to remove the pin that keeps the bands in place

Hand Motion:

Rolex watches have smooth and soundless second-hand motion, while fake watches have a ticking motion. While buying, look closely and listen carefully if it has a ticking sound, then it is a fake watch, not real. In Rolex watches, only the Oysterquartz is different; it uses a quartz movement, which causes it to tick like a quartz watch.

Cyclops Lens:

Real Rolex has a special lens called a “cyclops”.it’s shows the date as 2.5 times bigger. This lens on fake watches may have low quality and may not be aligned correctly or it may not magnify correctly. This feature of Cyclops is only available on real Rolex if you find another Rolex that has low quality lens that is not aligned correctly then it is fake maybe this type of watch falls in Frankenstein watches

Judge the Winding Crown :
